4.76.s:
nanda uvāca
yeṣāṃ ca darśane puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ yasya ca darśane .
tatsarva vada sarveśa śrotuṃ kautūharaṃ mama .. 1 ..
4.76.d:
नन्द उवाच
येषां च दर्शने पुण्यं पापं यस्य च दर्शने ।
तत्सर्व वद सर्वेश श्रोतुं कौतूहरं मम ॥ 1 ॥
4.76.m:
Now the seventy-sixth chapter.
Nanda said:
Tell me all about those whose sight brings merit, and whose sight brings sin, / O Lord of all; I have great curiosity to hear it. / 1

4.76.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
subrāhmaṇānāṃ tīrthānāṃ vaiṣṇavānāṃ ca darśane .
devatāpratimādarśī tīrthasnāyī bhavennaraḥ .. 2 ..
4.76.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
सुब्राह्मणानां तीर्थानां वैष्णवानां च दर्शने ।
देवताप्रतिमादर्शी तीर्थस्नायी भवेन्नरः ॥ 2 ॥
4.76.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
Upon seeing good Brahmins, sacred places, and Vaiṣṇavas, / a person who beholds the images of deities becomes [as one who has] bathed at a sacred place. / 2

4.76.s:
sūryasya darśane bhaktyā matīnāṃ darśane tathāḥ .
saṃnyāsināṃ yatīnāṃ ca tathaiva brahmacāriṇām .. 3 ..
4.76.d:
सूर्यस्य दर्शने भक्त्या मतीनां दर्शने तथाः ।
संन्यासिनां यतीनां च तथैव ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ॥ 3 ॥
4.76.m: Upon seeing the sun with devotion, and likewise seeing sages, / saṃnyāsins, ascetics, and likewise brahmacārins; / 3

4.76.s:
bhaktyā gavāṃ ca vahnīnāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .
gajendrāṇāṃ ca siṃhānāṃ śvetāśvānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 4 ..
4.76.d:
भक्त्या गवां च वह्नीनां गुरूणां च विशेषतः ।
गजेन्द्राणां च सिंहानां श्वेताश्वानां तथैव च ॥ 4 ॥
4.76.m: with devotion [seeing] cows and sacred fires, and especially gurus, / noble elephants, lions, and likewise white horses; / 4

4.76.s:
śukānāṃ ca pikānāṃ ca khañjanānāṃ tathaiva ca .
haṃsānāṃ ca mayūrāṇāṃ cāṣāṇāṃ śaṅkhapakṣiṇām .. 5 ..
4.76.d:
शुकानां च पिकानां च खञ्जनानां तथैव च ।
हंसानां च मयूराणां चाषाणां शङ्खपक्षिणाम् ॥ 5 ॥
4.76.m: parrots, cuckoos, and wagtails likewise, / swans, peacocks, blue jays, and conch-birds; / 5

4.76.s:
vatsaprayuktadhenūnāsaśvatthānāṃ tathaiva ca .
patiputravatīnāṃ ca narāṇāṃ tīnthayāyinām .. 6 ..
4.76.d:
वत्सप्रयुक्तधेनूनासश्वत्थानां तथैव च ।
पतिपुत्रवतीनां च नराणां तीन्थयायिनाम् ॥ 6 ॥
4.76.m: cows with their calves, and likewise sacred fig trees, / women with husband and sons, and men travelling to pilgrimage places; / 6

4.76.s:
pradīpānāṃ suvarṇānāṃ maṇīnāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .
ṇuktānāṃ hīrakāṇāṃ ca māṇikyānāṃ mahāśaya .. 7 ..
4.76.d:
प्रदीपानां सुवर्णानां मणीनां च विशेषतः ।
णुक्तानां हीरकाणां च माणिक्यानां महाशय ॥ 7 ॥
4.76.m: lamps, gold, and especially jewels, / pearls, diamonds, and rubies, O noble-minded one; / 7

4.76.s:
tulasīśuklapuṣpāṇāṃ darśanaṃ pāpanāśam .
phalāni śukladhānyāni ghṛtaṃ dadhi madhūni ca .. 8 ..
4.76.d:
तुलसीशुक्लपुष्पाणां दर्शनं पापनाशम् ।
फलानि शुक्लधान्यानि घृतं दधि मधूनि च ॥ 8 ॥
4.76.m: the sight of Tulasī and white flowers destroys sin; / fruits, white grains, clarified butter, curd, and honey; / 8

4.76.s:
pūrṇakumbhaṃ ca lājāṃśca rājendraṃ darpaṇaṃ jalam .
mālāṃ ca śuklapuṣpāṇāṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇyaṃ labhennaraḥ .. 9 ..
4.76.d:
पूर्णकुम्भं च लाजांश्च राजेन्द्रं दर्पणं जलम् ।
मालां च शुक्लपुष्पाणां दृष्ट्वा पुण्यं लभेन्नरः ॥ 9 ॥
4.76.m: a filled pitcher, parched grains, a noble king, a mirror, water, / and a garland of white flowers—having seen [these], a person obtains merit. / 9

4.76.s:
gorocanaṃ ca karpūraṃ rajataṃ ca sarovaram .
puṣpodyānaṃ puṣpitāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā puṇyaṃ labhennaraḥ .. 10 ..
4.76.d:
गोरोचनं च कर्पूरं रजतं च सरोवरम् ।
पुष्पोद्यानं पुष्पितां च दृष्ट्वा पुण्यं लभेन्नरः ॥ 10 ॥
4.76.m: Gorocanā, camphor, silver, and a lake, / a flower garden, and [a woman] in menses—having seen [these], a person obtains merit. / 10

4.76.s:
śuklapakṣasya candraṃ ca pīyūṣaṃ candanaṃ tathā .
kastūrīṃ kuṅkumaṃ dṛṣṭvā nanda puṇyaṃ .. 11 ..
4.76.d:
शुक्लपक्षस्य चन्द्रं च पीयूषं चन्दनं तथा ।
कस्तूरीं कुङ्कुमं दृष्ट्वा नन्द पुण्यं ॥ 11 ॥
4.76.m: The moon of the bright fortnight, nectar, and sandalwood, / musk, and saffron—having seen [these], O Nanda, [one obtains] merit. / 11

4.76.s:
patākāmakṣayavaṭaṃ taruṃ devotthitaṃ śubham .
devālayaṃ devakhātaṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇyaṃ labhennaraḥ .. 12 ..
4.76.d:
पताकामक्षयवटं तरुं देवोत्थितं शुभम् ।
देवालयं देवखातं दृष्ट्वा पुण्यं लभेन्नरः ॥ 12 ॥
4.76.m: A banner, the Imperishable Banyan, an auspicious tree sacred to a god, / a temple, and a sacred pond—having seen [these], a person obtains merit. / 12

4.76.s:
devākṣitāṃ devadyaṭaṃ sugandhipavanaṃ tathā .
śaṅkhaṃ ca duṃdubhiṃ dṛṣṭvā sadyaḥ puṇyaṃ labhennaraḥ .. 13 ..
4.76.d:
देवाक्षितां देवद्यटं सुगन्धिपवनं तथा ।
शङ्खं च दुंदुभिं दृष्ट्वा सद्यः पुण्यं लभेन्नरः ॥ 13 ॥
4.76.m: An image consecrated to a deity, a divine staff, and fragrant breeze, / a conch and a kettledrum—having seen [these], a person immediately obtains merit. / 13

4.76.s:
śukiṃta pravālaṃ rajataṃ sphaṭikaṃ kuśamūlakam .
gaṅgāmṛdaṃ kuśaṃ tāmraṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇyaṃ labhennaraḥ .. 14 ..
4.76.d:
शुकिंत प्रवालं रजतं स्फटिकं कुशमूलकम् ।
गङ्गामृदं कुशं ताम्रं दृष्ट्वा पुण्यं लभेन्नरः ॥ 14 ॥
4.76.m: An oyster shell, coral, silver, crystal, the root of kuśa grass, / soil from the Gaṅgā, kuśa grass, and copper—having seen [these], a person obtains merit. / 14

4.76.s:
purāṇapustakaṃ śuddhaṃ sabījaṃ viṣṇuyantrakam .
snigdhadūrvākṣate ratnaṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇyaṃ labhennaraḥ.. 15 ..
4.76.d:
पुराणपुस्तकं शुद्धं सबीजं विष्णुयन्त्रकम् ।
स्निग्धदूर्वाक्षते रत्नं दृष्ट्वा पुण्यं लभेन्नरः॥ 15 ॥
4.76.m: A pure book of the Purāṇas, an energized yantra of Viṣṇu, / unctuous dūrvā grass, unbroken rice, and a jewel—having seen [these], a person obtains merit. / 15

4.76.s:
tapasvināṃ siddhamantraṃ masudraṃ kṛṣṇasārakam .
yajñaṃ mahotsavaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa puṇyaṃ labhate naraḥ .. 16 ..
4.76.d:
तपस्विनां सिद्धमन्त्रं मसुद्रं कृष्णसारकम् ।
यज्ञं महोत्सवं दृष्ट्वा स पुण्यं लभते नरः ॥ 16 ॥
4.76.m: An accomplished mantra of ascetics, an ocean, a blackbuck, / a sacrificial rite, and a great festival—having seen [these], that person obtains merit. / 16

4.76.s:
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ dugdhaṃ godhūliṃ goṣṭhagoṣpadam .
pakvasasyānvitaṃ kṣetraṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇyaṃ labheddhruvam .. 17 ..
4.76.d:
गोमूत्रं गोमयं दुग्धं गोधूलिं गोष्ठगोष्पदम् ।
पक्वसस्यान्वितं क्षेत्रं दृष्ट्वा पुण्यं लभेद्ध्रुवम् ॥ 17 ॥
4.76.m: Cow urine, cow dung, milk, cow-dust, a cow-pen, and a cow's footprint, / a field filled with ripe crops—having seen [these], one surely obtains merit. / 17

4.76.s:
rucirāṃ padminīṃ śyāmāṃ nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalām .
suveṣakāṃ suvasanāṃ divyabhūṣaṇabhūṣitām .. 18 ..
4.76.d:
रुचिरां पद्मिनीं श्यामां न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डलाम् ।
सुवेषकां सुवसनां दिव्यभूषणभूषिताम् ॥ 18 ॥
4.76.m: A lovely lotus-like woman, youthful, with rounded limbs like a banyan tree, / finely dressed, well-clad, adorned with divine ornaments; / 18

4.76.s:
veśyāṃ kṣemakarīṃ gandhaṃ sudūrvākṣatataṇḍulam .
siddhānnaṃ paramānnaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā puṇyaṃ labhennaraḥ .. 19 ..
4.76.d:
वेश्यां क्षेमकरीं गन्धं सुदूर्वाक्षततण्डुलम् ।
सिद्धान्नं परमान्नं च दृष्ट्वा पुण्यं लभेन्नरः ॥ 19 ॥
4.76.m: a courtesan, an auspicious bird, fragrance, fine dūrvā grass, unbroken rice, / cooked food, and rice-milk—having seen [these], a person obtains merit. / 19

4.76.s:
kāntikyāṃ pūrṇimāyāṃ ca rādhikāpratimāṃ śubhām .
saṃpūjya dṛṣṭvā natvā ca karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 20 ..
4.76.d:
कान्तिक्यां पूर्णिमायां च राधिकाप्रतिमां शुभाम् ।
संपूज्य दृष्ट्वा नत्वा च करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 20 ॥
4.76.m: On the full-moon day of Kārttika, having worshipped, seen, / and bowed to the auspicious image of Rādhikā, one destroys rebirth. / 20

4.76.s:
hiṅgulāyāṃ tathā'ṣṭamyāmiṣe māsi site śubhe .
śrīdurgāpratimāṃ dṛṣṭvā karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 21 ..
4.76.d:
हिङ्गुलायां तथाऽष्टम्यामिषे मासि सिते शुभे ।
श्रीदुर्गाप्रतिमां दृष्ट्वा करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 21 ॥
4.76.m: At Hiṅgulā, on the auspicious bright eighth day in the month of Āśvina, / having seen the image of Śrī Durgā, one destroys rebirth. / 21

4.76.s:
śivarātrau ca kāśyāṃ ca viśvanāthasya darśanam .
kṛtvopavāsaṃ pūjāṃ ca karoti janmakhaṇḍanam.. 22 ..
4.76.d:
शिवरात्रौ च काश्यां च विश्वनाथस्य दर्शनम् ।
कृत्वोपवासं पूजां च करोति जन्मखण्डनम्॥ 22 ॥
4.76.m: On Śivarātri in Kāśī, having beheld Viśvanātha, / fasted, and performed worship, one destroys rebirth. / 22

4.76.s:
janmāṣṭamīdine bhakto dṛṣṭvā māṃ bindumādhavam .
praṇamya pūjāṃ kṛtvā ca karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 23 ..
4.76.d:
जन्माष्टमीदिने भक्तो दृष्ट्वा मां बिन्दुमाधवम् ।
प्रणम्य पूजां कृत्वा च करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 23 ॥
4.76.m: On the day of Janmāṣṭamī, a devotee, having seen me as Bindumādhava, / bowed down, and performed worship, destroys rebirth. / 23

4.76.s:
pauṣe māsi śuklarātrau yatra yatra sthale naraḥ .
padmāyāḥ pratimāṃ dṛṣṭvā karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 24 ..
4.76.d:
पौषे मासि शुक्लरात्रौ यत्र यत्र स्थले नरः ।
पद्मायाः प्रतिमां दृष्ट्वा करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 24 ॥
4.76.m: In the month of Pauṣa, on a bright night, wherever on earth a person / sees an image of Padmā, he destroys rebirth. / 24

4.76.s:
saptajanma bhavettasya putraḥ pautro dhaneśvaraḥ .
upoṣyaikādaśīṃ snātvā prabhāte dvādaśīdine .. 25 ..
4.76.d:
सप्तजन्म भवेत्तस्य पुत्रः पौत्रो धनेश्वरः ।
उपोष्यैकादशीं स्नात्वा प्रभाते द्वादशीदिने ॥ 25 ॥
4.76.m: For seven births his son and grandson become lords of wealth. / Having fasted on the eleventh day, and bathed at dawn on the twelfth day, / 25

4.76.s:
dṛṣṭvā kāśyāmannapūrṇāṃ karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .
caitrai māsi caturdaśyāṃ kāmarūpeṣu puṇyade .. 26 ..
4.76.d:
दृष्ट्वा काश्यामन्नपूर्णां करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ।
चैत्रै मासि चतुर्दश्यां कामरूपेषु पुण्यदे ॥ 26 ॥
4.76.m: and seen Annapūrṇā in Kāśī, one destroys rebirth. / In the month of Caitra, on the fourteenth day, in merit-bestowing Kāmarūpa, / 26

4.76.s:
dṛṣṭvā natvā bhadrakālīṃ karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .
ayodhyāyāṃ ca rāmaṃ ca śrīrāmanavamīdine .. 27 ..
4.76.d:
दृष्ट्वा नत्वा भद्रकालीं करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ।
अयोध्यायां च रामं च श्रीरामनवमीदिने ॥ 27 ॥
4.76.m: having seen and bowed to Bhadrakālī, one destroys rebirth. / In Ayodhyā, [having seen] Rāma on the day of Śrī Rāmanavamī, / 27

4.76.s:
saṃpūjya natvā dṛṣṭvā ca karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .
upoṣya puṣkare snātvā kiṃvā badarikāśrame .. 28 ..
4.76.d:
संपूज्य नत्वा दृष्ट्वा च करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ।
उपोष्य पुष्करे स्नात्वा किंवा बदरिकाश्रमे ॥ 28 ॥
4.76.m: having worshipped, bowed, and seen [him], one destroys rebirth. / Having fasted and bathed at Puṣkara or at Badarikāśrama, / 28

4.76.s:
maṃpūjya dṛṣṭvā māmekaṃ karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .
dattavā tiṣṇupade piṇḍaṃ viṣṇuṃ yaśca prapūjyet .. 29 ..
4.76.d:
मंपूज्य दृष्ट्वा मामेकं करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ।
दत्तवा तिष्णुपदे पिण्डं विष्णुं यश्च प्रपूज्येत् ॥ 29 ॥
4.76.m: having worshipped and seen me alone, one destroys rebirth. / Having offered a funeral cake at the footprint of Viṣṇu and worshipped Viṣṇu, / 29

4.76.s:
pitaṇāṃ svātmanaścaiva karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .
prayāge muṇḍanaṃ kṛtvā dānaṃ ca kurute yadi .. 30 ..
4.76.d:
पितणां स्वात्मनश्चैव करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ।
प्रयागे मुण्डनं कृत्वा दानं च कुरुते यदि ॥ 30 ॥
4.76.m: one destroys rebirth for one's ancestors and for oneself. / If, having shaved one's head at Prayāga, one makes gifts, / 30

4.76.s:
upoṣya naimiṣāraṇye karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .
siddhiṃ kṛtvā ca vadarīṃbhuṅkte badarikāśrame .. 31 ..
4.76.d:
उपोष्य नैमिषारण्ये करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ।
सिद्धिं कृत्वा च वदरींभुङ्क्ते बदरिकाश्रमे ॥ 31 ॥
4.76.m: and having fasted in Naimiṣāraṇya, one destroys rebirth. / Having attained perfection, eating jujube fruit at Badarikāśrama, / 31

4.76.s:
dṛṣṭavā matpratimāṃ nanda karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .
delāyamānaṃ govindaṃ puṇye vṛndāvane ca mām .. 32 ..
4.76.d:
दृष्टवा मत्प्रतिमां नन्द करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ।
देलायमानं गोविन्दं पुण्ये वृन्दावने च माम् ॥ 32 ॥
4.76.m: and having seen my image, O Nanda, one destroys rebirth. / [Seeing] me, Govinda, swinging in holy Vṛndāvana— / 32

4.76.s:
dṛṣṭavā saṃpūjya natvā ca karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .
bhādre dṛṣṭvā ca mañcasthaṃ māmeva madhusūdanam .. 33 ..
4.76.d:
दृष्टवा संपूज्य नत्वा च करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ।
भाद्रे दृष्ट्वा च मञ्चस्थं मामेव मधुसूदनम् ॥ 33 ॥
4.76.m: having seen, worshipped, and bowed to me, one destroys rebirth. / In the month of Bhādra, having seen me, Madhusūdana, on the dais, / 33

4.76.s:
saṃpūjya natvā bhaktaśca karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .
rathasthaṃ ca jagannāthaṃ yo drakṣyati kalau naraḥ ..
saṃpūjya natvā bhaktyā ca karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 34 ..
4.76.d:
संपूज्य नत्वा भक्तश्च करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ।
रथस्थं च जगन्नाथं यो द्रक्ष्यति कलौ नरः ॥
संपूज्य नत्वा भक्त्या च करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 34 ॥
4.76.m:
a devotee, having worshipped and bowed, destroys rebirth. / In the Kali age, whatever person sees Jagannātha on the chariot,
and having worshipped and bowed with devotion, destroys rebirth. / 34

4.76.s:
uttarāyaṇasaṃkrāntyāṃ prayāge snānamācaret .
saṃpūjya natvā māmeva karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 35 ..
4.76.d:
उत्तरायणसंक्रान्त्यां प्रयागे स्नानमाचरेत् ।
संपूज्य नत्वा मामेव करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.76.m: At the winter solstice, one should bathe at Prayāga; / having worshipped and bowed to me alone, one destroys rebirth. / 35

4.76.s:
kārtikyāṃ pūrṇimāyāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā matpratimāṃ śubhām .
upoṣya pūjaraṃ kṛtvā karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 36 ..
4.76.d:
कार्तिक्यां पूर्णिमायां च दृष्ट्वा मत्प्रतिमां शुभाम् ।
उपोष्य पूजरं कृत्वा करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 36 ॥
4.76.m: On the full-moon day of Kārttika, having seen my auspicious image, / fasted, and performed worship, one destroys rebirth. / 36

4.76.s:
candrabhāgāsamīpe ca mādhyāṃ ca māṃ nametsudhīḥ .
rādhayā saha māṃ dṛṣṭvā karoti janmanaḥ kṣayam .. 37 ..
4.76.d:
चन्द्रभागासमीपे च माध्यां च मां नमेत्सुधीः ।
राधया सह मां दृष्ट्वा करोति जन्मनः क्षयम् ॥ 37 ॥
4.76.m: Near the Candrabhāgā on the full-moon day of Māgha, a wise person should bow to me; / having seen me together with Rādhā, he causes the destruction of rebirth. / 37

4.76.s:
rāmeśvaraṃ setubandha aṣāṇīpūrṇimādine .
upeṣya dṛṣṭvā saṃpūjya karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 38 ..
4.76.d:
रामेश्वरं सेतुबन्ध अषाणीपूर्णिमादिने ।
उपेष्य दृष्ट्वा संपूज्य करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.76.m: At Rāmeśvara on the bridge on the full-moon day of Āṣāḍha, / having fasted, seen, and worshipped, one destroys rebirth. / 38

4.76.s:
svarge vidyādharā rātrau nṛtyanti ca suhurmuhuḥ.
praṇāmaṃ kartumīśaṃ taṃ samāyāti vibhīṣaṇaḥ .. 39 ..
4.76.d:
स्वर्गे विद्याधरा रात्रौ नृत्यन्ति च सुहुर्मुहुः।
प्रणामं कर्तुमीशं तं समायाति विभीषणः ॥ 39 ॥
4.76.m: In heaven, the Vidyādharas dance constantly at night; / and Vibhīṣaṇa arrives to offer obeisance to that Lord.

4.76.s:
gāyanti kiṃnarā rātrau gandharvāśca manoharam .
praṇāmaṃ kartumīśaṃ ta samāyāti ya mādhavaḥ .. 40 ..
4.76.d:
गायन्ति किंनरा रात्रौ गन्धर्वाश्च मनोहरम् ।
प्रणामं कर्तुमीशं त समायाति य माधवः ॥ 40 ॥
4.76.m: At night, the Kiṃnaras and Gandharvas sing delightfully; / and Mādhava arrives to offer obeisance to that Lord.

4.76.s:
dṛṣṭvā sākṣādvasantaṃ ca sarveśaṃ candraśekharam .
jīvanmukto bhavedante prayāti harimandiram .. 41 ..
4.76.d:
दृष्ट्वा साक्षाद्वसन्तं च सर्वेशं चन्द्रशेखरम् ।
जीवन्मुक्तो भवेदन्ते प्रयाति हरिमन्दिरम् ॥ 41 ॥
4.76.m: Beholding the Lord of all, who wears the crescent moon, dwelling manifestly in person, / one becomes liberated while living, and in the end goes to the abode of Hari.

4.76.s:
dīnanāthaṃ dinakaraṃ koṇārke cottarāyaṇe .
upoṣya dṛṣṭvā saṃpūjya karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 42 ..
4.76.d:
दीननाथं दिनकरं कोणार्के चोत्तरायणे ।
उपोष्य दृष्ट्वा संपूज्य करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.76.m: At Koṇārka on the northern solstice, having fasted, / beholding and worshipping the sun, the protector of the distressed, one destroys all births.

4.76.s:
kṛṣikoṣṭhe suvasane kalarvike vasuṃdhare .
vispandake rājakoṣṭhe nandake puṣpabhadrake .. 43 ..
4.76.d:
कृषिकोष्ठे सुवसने कलर्विके वसुंधरे ।
विस्पन्दके राजकोष्ठे नन्दके पुष्पभद्रके ॥ 43 ॥
4.76.m: At Kṛṣikoṣṭha, Suvasana, Kalarvika, Vasuṃdhara, / Vispandaka, Rājakoṣṭha, Nandaka, and Puṣpabhadraka—

4.76.s:
pārvatīpratimāṃ dṛṣṭvā kārtikeyaṃ gaṇeśvaram .
nandinaṃ śaṃkaraṃ dṛṣṭvā karoti janmanaḥ kṣayam .. 44 ..
4.76.d:
पार्वतीप्रतिमां दृष्ट्वा कार्तिकेयं गणेश्वरम् ।
नन्दिनं शंकरं दृष्ट्वा करोति जन्मनः क्षयम् ॥ 44 ॥
4.76.m: beholding the image of Pārvatī, Kārtikeya, Gaṇeśvara, / Nandin, and Śaṅkara, one destroys further birth.

4.76.s:
upoṣya prātaḥ saṃpūjya dṛṣṭvā stutvā stutau nataḥ .
pāraṇaṃ ca dadhi prāśya karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 45 ..
4.76.d:
उपोष्य प्रातः संपूज्य दृष्ट्वा स्तुत्वा स्तुतौ नतः ।
पारणं च दधि प्राश्य करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 45 ॥
4.76.m: Having fasted, worshipped in the morning, beheld [them], and praised [them] with bowed head in a hymn of praise, / and breaking the fast by tasting curd, one severs cycle of rebirth.

4.76.s:
trikūṭe maṇibhadre ca paścimodadhisaṃnidhau .
samupoṣya dadhi praśya māṃ dṛṣṭvā muktimāpnuyāt .. 46 ..
4.76.d:
त्रिकूटे मणिभद्रे च पश्चिमोदधिसंनिधौ ।
समुपोष्य दधि प्रश्य मां दृष्ट्वा मुक्तिमाप्नुयात् ॥ 46 ॥
4.76.m: At Trikūṭa and Maṇibhadra near the western ocean, / having fasted, tasting curd, and beholding me, one attains liberation.

4.76.s:
pratimāsu madīyāsu pārvatīpratimāsu ca .
jīvaṃ saṃnyasya saṃpūjya karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 47 ..
4.76.d:
प्रतिमासु मदीयासु पार्वतीप्रतिमासु च ।
जीवं संन्यस्य संपूज्य करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 47 ॥
4.76.m: Infusing life into my images and into the images of Pārvatī / and worshipping them, one destroys further birth.

4.76.s:
śivadurgālayaṃ kṛtvā madīyaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .
śivasaṃsthāpanaṃ kṛtvā karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 48 ..
4.76.d:
शिवदुर्गालयं कृत्वा मदीयं च विशेषतः ।
शिवसंस्थापनं कृत्वा करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 48 ॥
4.76.m: Having built an abode for Śiva and Durgā, and especially for me, / and having installed Śiva, one destroys further birth.

4.76.s:
puṣpodyānaṃ ca śaṃkuṃ ca setuṃ khātaṃ sarovaram .
viprasaṃsthāpanaṃ kṛtvā karoti janmakhaṇḍanam .. 49 ..
4.76.d:
पुष्पोद्यानं च शंकुं च सेतुं खातं सरोवरम् ।
विप्रसंस्थापनं कृत्वा करोति जन्मखण्डनम् ॥ 49 ॥
4.76.m: Having provided a flower garden, a stake, a bridge, an excavation, and a lake, / and having established Brahmins, one destroys further birth.

4.76.s:
na ca vedāḥ purāṇāni brahmasaṃsthāpanaṃ phalam .
jānanti santo munayaḥ surā viprādayaḥ pitaḥ .. 50 ..
4.76.d:
न च वेदाः पुराणानि ब्रह्मसंस्थापनं फलम् ।
जानन्ति सन्तो मुनयः सुरा विप्रादयः पितः ॥ 50 ॥
4.76.m: Neither the Vedas nor the Purāṇas know the fruit of establishing Brahmins, / O father, nor do the virtuous, the sages, the gods, or Brahmins and others.

4.76.s:
gaṇyante pāṃsavo bhūmergaṇyante vṛṣṭibindavaḥ .
na gaṇyate vidhātrā'pi viprasaṃsthāpane phalam .. 51 ..
4.76.d:
गण्यन्ते पांसवो भूमेर्गण्यन्ते वृष्टिबिन्दवः ।
न गण्यते विधात्राऽपि विप्रसंस्थापने फलम् ॥ 51 ॥
4.76.m: The particles of dust on the earth may be counted, the raindrops may be counted, / but the fruit of establishing a Brahmin is not counted even by the Creator.

4.76.s:
kṛtvopajīṃyaṃ viprasya jīvanmukto bhavennaraḥ .
acalāṃ śrīyamāpnoti pare sukticatuṣṭayam .. 52 ..
4.76.d:
कृत्वोपजींयं विप्रस्य जीवन्मुक्तो भवेन्नरः ।
अचलां श्रीयमाप्नोति परे सुक्तिचतुष्टयम् ॥ 52 ॥
4.76.m: Having provided a livelihood for a Brahmin, a man becomes liberated while living; / he attains unwavering fortune, and hereafter the fourfold liberation.

4.76.s:
maddāsyabhaktiṃ sa labhedvaikuṇṭhe modake ciram .
na hi pāto bhavettasya yathā me paramātmanaḥ .. 53 ..
4.76.d:
मद्दास्यभक्तिं स लभेद्वैकुण्ठे मोदके चिरम् ।
न हि पातो भवेत्तस्य यथा मे परमात्मनः ॥ 53 ॥
4.76.m: He attains devotion characterised by servitude to me, and rejoices long in Vaikuṇṭha; / indeed, there is no fall for him, just as there is none for me, the Paramātman.

4.76.s:
kumārīmaṣṭavarṣoyāṃ suvipraya dadāti yaḥ .
saṃpūjya sarvābharaṇāṃ durgādānaphalaṃ labhet .. 54 ..
4.76.d:
कुमारीमष्टवर्षोयां सुविप्रय ददाति यः ।
संपूज्य सर्वाभरणां दुर्गादानफलं लभेत् ॥ 54 ॥
4.76.m: He who gives an eight-year-old maiden to an excellent Brahmin, / worshipping her adorned with all ornaments, obtains the fruit of giving Durgā.

4.76.s:
sarva svargya samālokya brahmalokeṣu pūjitaḥ .
labhate mama dāsyaṃ ca vaisuṇṭhe modate ciram .. 55 ..
4.76.d:
सर्व स्वर्ग्य समालोक्य ब्रह्मलोकेषु पूजितः ।
लभते मम दास्यं च वैसुण्ठे मोदते चिरम् ॥ 55 ॥
4.76.m: Having looked upon all heaven, revered in the worlds of Brahmā, / he obtains servitude to me and rejoices long in Vaikuṇṭha.

4.76.s:
vivāhadarśane koṭisvarṇadānaphalaṃ labhet .
ante svarge prayātyevamihaiva niścalāṃ śriyam .. 56 ..
4.76.d:
विवाहदर्शने कोटिस्वर्णदानफलं लभेत् ।
अन्ते स्वर्गे प्रयात्येवमिहैव निश्चलां श्रियम् ॥ 56 ॥
4.76.m: By witnessing a wedding, one obtains the fruit of giving ten million gold pieces; / in the end he goes to heaven, and in this world attains unwavering fortune.

4.76.s:
yaḥ suvipramanāthaṃ ca daridraṃ ca supaṇa़ḍitam .
dṛṣṭvā kuryāttadvivāhaṃ sa mokṣaṃ labhate dhruvam .. 57 ..
4.76.d:
यः सुविप्रमनाथं च दरिद्रं च सुपण़डितम् ।
दृष्ट्वा कुर्यात्तद्विवाहं स मोक्षं लभते ध्रुवम् ॥ 57 ॥
4.76.m: He who, seeing an excellent Brahmin who is helpless, poor, and very learned, / arranges his marriage, surely attains liberation.

4.76.s:
yacchatrapādukādānaṃ śālagrāmasya yoṣitaḥ .
karoti bhaktyā puṇyāhe pṛthvīdānaphalaṃ labhet .. 58 ..
4.76.d:
यच्छत्रपादुकादानं शालग्रामस्य योषितः ।
करोति भक्त्या पुण्याहे पृथ्वीदानफलं लभेत् ॥ 58 ॥
4.76.m: He who with devotion gives an umbrella and sandals to a woman with a Śāligrāma / on an auspicious day, obtains the fruit of gifting the earth.

4.76.s:
gajacadāne ca tallomamānavarṣa śrutau śrutam .
caturguṇaṃ gajendraṃ ca modate mama mandire .. 59 ..
4.76.d:
गजचदाने च तल्लोममानवर्ष श्रुतौ श्रुतम् ।
चतुर्गुणं गजेन्द्रं च मोदते मम मन्दिरे ॥ 59 ॥
4.76.m: In the gift of an elephant, [he rejoices] for as many years as its hairs—so is heard in the Veda; / for four times that in the gift of a lordly elephant, he rejoices in my abode.

4.76.s:
gajardha śvetaturage tadardha cetane pitaḥ .
gajatulyaṃ kṛṣṇagavāṃ dāne ca tatphalaṃ labhet .. 60 ..
4.76.d:
गजर्ध श्वेततुरगे तदर्ध चेतने पितः ।
गजतुल्यं कृष्णगवां दाने च तत्फलं लभेत् ॥ 60 ॥
4.76.m: Half that of an elephant for a white horse, and half of that for a living [animal], O father; / and in the gift of black cows, one obtains the fruit equal to an elephant.

4.76.s:
tattulyaṃ dhenudāne ca hyardhaṃ sāmānyagostathā .
labhedvatsaprasūtānāṃ dāne dāne phalaṃ bhuvaḥ .. 61 ..
4.76.d:
तत्तुल्यं धेनुदाने च ह्यर्धं सामान्यगोस्तथा ।
लभेद्वत्सप्रसूतानां दाने दाने फलं भुवः ॥ 61 ॥
4.76.m: Equal to that in the gift of a milch cow, and half of that for an ordinary cow; / in the gift of cows that have newly given birth to calves, one obtains each time the fruit of gifting the earth.

4.76.s:
bhūmidāne reṇumānavarṣa sthānaṃ ca matpade .
jñānadāne mahatpuṇyaṃ vaikuṇṭhe modate ciram .. 62 ..
4.76.d:
भूमिदाने रेणुमानवर्ष स्थानं च मत्पदे ।
ज्ञानदाने महत्पुण्यं वैकुण्ठे मोदते चिरम् ॥ 62 ॥
4.76.m: In the gift of land, one stays at my abode for as many years as there are particles of dust; / in the gift of knowledge, there is great merit, and one rejoices long in Vaikuṇṭha.

4.76.s:
śriyaṃ labhetsvarṇadāne rājatvaṃ rajatena ca .
annadāne phalaṃ gahaṃ kathaṃ jānāmi pai śutam .. 63 ..
4.76.d:
श्रियं लभेत्स्वर्णदाने राजत्वं रजतेन च ।
अन्नदाने फलं गहं कथं जानामि पै शुतम् ॥ 63 ॥
4.76.m: In the gift of gold, one obtains fortune, and sovereignty through silver; / how can I comprehend the deep fruit in the gift of food, O father, as heard?

4.76.s:
labhate sarvadānasya phalaṃ brahmaṇabhojane .
annadānātparaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati .. 64 ..
4.76.d:
लभते सर्वदानस्य फलं ब्रह्मणभोजने ।
अन्नदानात्परं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति ॥ 64 ॥
4.76.m: In feeding Brahmins, one obtains the fruit of all gifts; / there is no gift greater than the gift of food, neither has there been, nor will there be.

4.76.s:
nātra pātraparīkṣā'sti na kālaniyamaḥ kvacit .
annadāne śubhaṃ puṇyaṃ dātuḥ pātraṃ tvapātakī .. 65 ..
4.76.d:
नात्र पात्रपरीक्षाऽस्ति न कालनियमः क्वचित् ।
अन्नदाने शुभं पुण्यं दातुः पात्रं त्वपातकी ॥ 65 ॥
4.76.m: Here there is no examination of the recipient, nor any restriction of time anywhere; / auspicious merit arises in the gift of food, provided the recipient of the giver is free from sin.

4.76.s:
annadānaṃ ca dhanyaṃ syādbhūmau vaikuṇṭhahetukam .
vastraṃ dadāti vipraya daridrāya kuṭumbine .. 66 ..
4.76.d:
अन्नदानं च धन्यं स्याद्भूमौ वैकुण्ठहेतुकम् ।
वस्त्रं ददाति विप्रय दरिद्राय कुटुम्बिने ॥ 66 ॥
4.76.m: The gift of food is blessed on earth, the cause of attaining Vaikuṇṭha. / If one gives cloth to a Brahmin who is poor and has a family,

4.76.s:
vastraṃsūtramānavarṣa vaikuṇṭhe modate ciram .
suramye candraloke ca vāruṇe ca tathaiva ca .. 67 ..
4.76.d:
वस्त्रंसूत्रमानवर्ष वैकुण्ठे मोदते चिरम् ।
सुरम्ये चन्द्रलोके च वारुणे च तथैव च ॥ 67 ॥
4.76.m: he rejoices long in Vaikuṇṭha for as many years as the threads of the cloth, / and likewise in the delightful world of the Moon and the world of Varuṇa.

4.76.s:
kṛtvā lohapradīpaṃ ca svarṇavartisamanvitam .
dattavā ghṛtapradīpaṃ ca haraye paramātmane .. 68 ..
4.76.d:
कृत्वा लोहप्रदीपं च स्वर्णवर्तिसमन्वितम् ।
दत्तवा घृतप्रदीपं च हरये परमात्मने ॥ 68 ॥
4.76.m: Having made an iron lamp provided with a golden wick, / and having offered a lamp of ghee to Hari, the Paramātman,

4.76.s:
andhakāraṃ ca na gṛhaṃ yamadūtaṃ yamaṃ tathā .
na hi paśyati dātā ca prayāti mama mandiram .. 69 ..
4.76.d:
अन्धकारं च न गृहं यमदूतं यमं तथा ।
न हि पश्यति दाता च प्रयाति मम मन्दिरम् ॥ 69 ॥
4.76.m: the giver does not see a house of darkness, nor Yama's messenger, nor Yama; / he goes directly to my abode.

4.76.s:
brahmaṇāya ca dattavaiva na yāti yamayātanām .
divyavarṣasahaśraṃ ca modate śakramandire .. 70 ..
4.76.d:
ब्रह्मणाय च दत्तवैव न याति यमयातनाम् ।
दिव्यवर्षसहश्रं च मोदते शक्रमन्दिरे ॥ 70 ॥
4.76.m: Having given it to a Brahmin, he does not go to the torments of Yama; / he rejoices in the abode of Śakra for a thousand divine years.

4.76.s:
āsanaṃ labhate svarge vastumātrānurūpataḥ .
uttame lakṣavarṣe ca tadardha cetare vrajet .. 71 ..
4.76.d:
आसनं लभते स्वर्गे वस्तुमात्रानुरूपतः ।
उत्तमे लक्षवर्षे च तदर्ध चेतरे व्रजेत् ॥ 71 ॥
4.76.m: One receives a seat in heaven in accordance with the measure of the object: / for an excellent one, for a hundred thousand years; and for another, he goes for half that time.

4.76.s:
tāmpūlena labhedbhogaṃ svarge varṣaśataṃ vrajet .
mālyadāne priyaṃ svarga vastumātrānurūpataḥ .. 72 ..
4.76.d:
ताम्पूलेन लभेद्भोगं स्वर्गे वर्षशतं व्रजेत् ।
माल्यदाने प्रियं स्वर्ग वस्तुमात्रानुरूपतः ॥ 72 ॥
4.76.m: Through betel, one receives enjoyment and goes to heaven for a hundred years; / in giving a garland, heaven is pleasing, in accordance with the measure of the object.

4.76.s:
phaladānaphalaṃ svarga labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ .
sāmānyaśayyādānena svarga varṣaśataṃ vrajet .. 73 ..
4.76.d:
फलदानफलं स्वर्ग लभते नात्र संशयः ।
सामान्यशय्यादानेन स्वर्ग वर्षशतं व्रजेत् ॥ 73 ॥
4.76.m: One obtains heaven as the fruit of giving fruit, there is no doubt of this; / by giving an ordinary bed, one goes to heaven for a hundred years.

4.76.s:
caturguṇaṃ prakṛṣṭāyāṃ guṇalakṣaṃ dilakṣaṇe .
anāthāya suviprāya yadi gehaṃ pradīyate .. 74 ..
4.76.d:
चतुर्गुणं प्रकृष्टायां गुणलक्षं दिलक्षणे ।
अनाथाय सुविप्राय यदि गेहं प्रदीयते ॥ 74 ॥
4.76.m: Fourfold for an excellent [bed], and a hundred thousandfold for an extraordinary one. / If a house is given to an orphaned, excellent Brahmin,

4.76.s:
atraiva mānavarṣa ca śakraloke mahīyate .
dṛṣṭvā bubhukṣitaṃ vipramannaṃ tasmai pradīyate .. 75 ..
4.76.d:
अत्रैव मानवर्ष च शक्रलोके महीयते ।
दृष्ट्वा बुभुक्षितं विप्रमन्नं तस्मै प्रदीयते ॥ 75 ॥
4.76.m: he is honoured in the world of Śakra for as many human years. / Seeing a hungry Brahmin, food is given to him—

4.76.s:
ayalāṃ śriyamāpnoti putrapautravivardhinīm .
vrajanātha vrajaṃ gatvā vrajabhūmau vrajādhunā .. 76 ..
4.76.d:
अयलां श्रियमाप्नोति पुत्रपौत्रविवर्धिनीम् ।
व्रजनाथ व्रजं गत्वा व्रजभूमौ व्रजाधुना ॥ 76 ॥
4.76.m: one attains unwavering fortune that increases sons and grandsons. / O Lord of Vraja, having gone to Vraja, go now to the land of Vraja!

4.76.s:
vraja bhojaya vipāṃśca vraja sarva vraje vraje .
gokule gokule vatsa vatsa vatsa nirākule .. 77 ..
4.76.d:
व्रज भोजय विपांश्च व्रज सर्व व्रजे व्रजे ।
गोकुले गोकुले वत्स वत्स वत्स निराकुले ॥ 77 ॥
4.76.m: Go, feed the Brahmins, go, [give] everything in Vraja after Vraja, / in cowherd settlement after cowherd settlement, O dear child, free from distress,

4.76.s:
vyākulānāṃ gokulānāṃ saṃkule ca vraje vraje .
etatte kathitaṃ nanda sānandaṃ puṇyavardhanam ..
susvapnadarśanaṃ puṇyaṃ yadi nīcaṃ na vakti ca .. 78 ..
4.76.d:
व्याकुलानां गोकुलानां संकुले च व्रजे व्रजे ।
एतत्ते कथितं नन्द सानन्दं पुण्यवर्धनम् ॥
सुस्वप्नदर्शनं पुण्यं यदि नीचं न वक्ति च ॥ 78 ॥
4.76.m:
in the thronged Vraja amidst the distressed cowherd settlements. / This has been told to you, O Nanda, joyful and increasing merit.
The seeing of an auspicious dream is meritorious, if one does not speak of it to a low person.

4.76.s:
kāśyapaṃ durbhagaṃ nīcaṃ śatrumajñāninaṃ streyam .
tyaktvā rātriṃ ca divase vakti vipraṃ mupaṇḍitam .. 79 ..
4.76.d:
काश्यपं दुर्भगं नीचं शत्रुमज्ञानिनं स्त्रेयम् ।
त्यक्त्वा रात्रिं च दिवसे वक्ति विप्रं मुपण्डितम् ॥ 79 ॥
4.76.m: Avoiding a descendant of Kaśyapa, an unfortunate person, a low person, an enemy, an ignorant person, or a woman, / and avoiding the night, one tells it by day to a learned Brahmin.

4.76.s:
devālaye ca devaṃ vā'pyaśvatthatulaśīvaṭam .
uktvā taddviguṇaṃ puṇyamaprakāśya caturguṇam .. 80 ..
4.76.d:
देवालये च देवं वाऽप्यश्वत्थतुलशीवटम् ।
उक्त्वा तद्द्विगुणं पुण्यमप्रकाश्य चतुर्गुणम् ॥ 80 ॥
4.76.m: Or having told it in a temple to a deity, or to an aśvattha tree, tulasī, or banyan tree, / the merit is twofold; keeping it undisclosed, it is fourfold.

4.76.s:
susvapnadarśane prājño gaṃgāsnānaphalaṃ labhet .
arthaṃ vittaṃ ca bhāryā ca bhūmiṃ putraṃ labhetprajām .. 81 ..
4.76.d:
सुस्वप्नदर्शने प्राज्ञो गंगास्नानफलं लभेत् ।
अर्थं वित्तं च भार्या च भूमिं पुत्रं लभेत्प्रजाम् ॥ 81 ॥
4.76.m: Upon seeing an auspicious dream, the wise man obtains the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā; / he obtains wealth, riches, a wife, land, a son, and offspring.

4.76.s:
mokṣaṃ ca paramaiśvaryaṃ labhate sarvavāñchitam .
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ tāta kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi .. 82 ..
iti śrībrahmao mahāo śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhao uttao nāradanāo bhagavannandasaṃo
ṣaṭsaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 76 ..
4.76.d:
मोक्षं च परमैश्वर्यं लभते सर्ववाञ्छितम् ।
इत्येवं कथितं तात किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ 82 ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्मओ महाओ श्रीकृष्णजन्मखओ उत्तओ नारदनाओ भगवन्नन्दसंओ
षट्सप्ततितमोऽध्यायः ॥ 76 ॥
4.76.m:
He attains liberation, supreme sovereignty, and all that is desired. / Thus this has been spoken to you, dear father; what more do you wish to hear?
Thus ends the seventy-sixth chapter in the dialogue between Nārada and Nārāyaṇa, [in the conversation between] the Lord and Nanda, in the Śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍa of the glorious Mahā-Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa. 76.

4.77.s:
nanda uvāca
kena spapnena kiṃ puṇyaṃ kena mokṣo bhavetsukham .
ko'pi ko'pi ca susvapnastatsarvaṃ kathaya prabho .. 1 ..
4.77.d:
नन्द उवाच
केन स्पप्नेन किं पुण्यं केन मोक्षो भवेत्सुखम् ।
कोऽपि कोऽपि च सुस्वप्नस्तत्सर्वं कथय प्रभो ॥ 1 ॥
4.77.m:
Now the seventy-seventh chapter.
Nanda said:
By which dream does what merit arise? By which does liberation [and] happiness come about?
Whatever good dreams there may be, tell me all of that, O Lord! 1.

4.77.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
vedeṣu sāmavedaśca praśastaḥ sarvakarmasu .
tathaiva kaṇvaśākhāyāṃ puṇyakāṇḍe manohare .. 2 ..
4.77.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
वेदेषु सामवेदश्च प्रशस्तः सर्वकर्मसु ।
तथैव कण्वशाखायां पुण्यकाण्डे मनोहरे ॥ 2 ॥

4.77.s:
sa vyavato yaśca duḥsvapnaḥ śaśvatapuṇyaphalapradaḥ .
tatsarva nikhilaṃ tāta kathayāmi niśāmaya .. 3 ..
4.77.d:
स व्यवतो यश्च दुःस्वप्नः शश्वतपुण्यफलप्रदः ।
तत्सर्व निखिलं तात कथयामि निशामय ॥ 3 ॥
4.77.m:
[it is explained] which bad dream yields perpetual fruits of merit.
Listen, father, I shall tell you all of that in full. 3.

4.77.s:
svapnādhyāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi bahupuṇyaphalapradam .
svapnādhyāyaṃ naraḥ śrutvā gaṅgāsnānaphalaṃ labhet .. 4 ..
4.77.d:
स्वप्नाध्यायं प्रवक्ष्यामि बहुपुण्यफलप्रदम् ।
स्वप्नाध्यायं नरः श्रुत्वा गङ्गास्नानफलं लभेत् ॥ 4 ॥
4.77.m:
I shall explain the chapter on dreams, which grants the fruits of much merit.
Hearing the chapter on dreams, a person attains the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā. 4.

4.77.s:
svapnaktu prathame yāme saṃvatsaraphalapradaḥ .
dvitīye cāṣṭabhirmāsaistribhirmāsaistṛtīyare .. 5 ..
4.77.d:
स्वप्नक्तु प्रथमे यामे संवत्सरफलप्रदः ।
द्वितीये चाष्टभिर्मासैस्त्रिभिर्मासैस्तृतीयरे ॥ 5 ॥
4.77.m:
A dream in the first watch gives its fruit within a year;
in the second, within eight months; in the third, within three months; 5.

4.77.s:
caturthe cārdhamāsena svapnaḥ svātmaphalapradaḥ .
daśāhe phaladaḥ svapno'pyaruṇodayadarṇane .. 6 ..
4.77.d:
चतुर्थे चार्धमासेन स्वप्नः स्वात्मफलप्रदः ।
दशाहे फलदः स्वप्नोऽप्यरुणोदयदर्णने ॥ 6 ॥
4.77.m:
and in the fourth, a dream brings about its fruit in half a month.
Seen at dawn, a dream gives its fruit in ten days. 6.

4.77.s:
prātaḥsvapnaśca phaladastatkṣaṇaṃ yadi bodhitaḥ .
dine manasi yaddṛṣṭaṃ tatsarva ca labheddhruvam .. 7 ..
4.77.d:
प्रातःस्वप्नश्च फलदस्तत्क्षणं यदि बोधितः ।
दिने मनसि यद्दृष्टं तत्सर्व च लभेद्ध्रुवम् ॥ 7 ॥
4.77.m:
A morning dream brings its fruit immediately if one wakes up [then].
Whatever was seen in the mind during the day, all that one certainly obtains. 7.

4.77.s:
cintāvyādhisamāyukto naraḥ svapnaṃ ca paśyati .
tatsarva niṣphalaṃ tāta prayātyeva na saṃśayaḥ .. 8 ..
4.77.d:
चिन्ताव्याधिसमायुक्तो नरः स्वप्नं च पश्यति ।
तत्सर्व निष्फलं तात प्रयात्येव न संशयः ॥ 8 ॥
4.77.m:
A person afflicted with anxiety or disease who sees a dream—
all that goes in vain, father, without a doubt. 8.

4.77.s:
jacaḍo mūtrapurīṣeṇa pīḍitaśca bhayākulaḥ .
digambaro muktakeśo na labhetsvapnajaṃ phalam .. 9 ..
4.77.d:
जचडो मूत्रपुरीषेण पीडितश्च भयाकुलः ।
दिगम्बरो मुक्तकेशो न लभेत्स्वप्नजं फलम् ॥ 9 ॥
4.77.m:
One who is dull-witted, troubled by urine or feces, terrified,
naked, or having disheveled hair does not attain the fruit born of a dream. 9.

4.77.s:
dṛṣṭvā svapnaṃ ca nidrāluryadi nidrāṃ prayati ca .
vimūḍho vakti cedrātrau na labhetsvapnajaṃ phalam .. 10 ..
4.77.d:
दृष्ट्वा स्वप्नं च निद्रालुर्यदि निद्रां प्रयति च ।
विमूढो वक्ति चेद्रात्रौ न लभेत्स्वप्नजं फलम् ॥ 10 ॥
4.77.m:
If a sleepy person, having seen a dream, goes back to sleep,
or if a fool recounts it at night, he does not attain the fruit born of a dream. 10.

4.77.s:
uktavā kāśyapagotre ca vipartti labhate dhruvam .
durgate durgatiṃ yāti nīce vyādhiṃprayāti ca .. 11 ..
4.77.d:
उक्तवा काश्यपगोत्रे च विपर्त्ति लभते ध्रुवम् ।
दुर्गते दुर्गतिं याति नीचे व्याधिंप्रयाति च ॥ 11 ॥
4.77.m:
Having spoken it to one of the Kāśyapa lineage, he certainly meets with misfortune;
to a wretched person, he goes to distress; to a lowborn person, he goes to disease; 11.

4.77.s:
śatrau bhayaṃ ca labhate mūrkhe ca kalahaṃ labhet .
kāminyāṃ dhanahāniḥ syādrātrau jorabhayaṃ bhavet .. 12 ..
4.77.d:
शत्रौ भयं च लभते मूर्खे च कलहं लभेत् ।
कामिन्यां धनहानिः स्याद्रात्रौ जोरभयं भवेत् ॥ 12 ॥
4.77.m:
to an enemy, he obtains fear; to a fool, he incurs conflict;
to a wanton woman, loss of wealth will result; at night, there will be fear of thieves; 12.

4.77.s:
nidrāyāṃ labhate śokaṃ paṇa़ḍite vāñchitaṃ phalam .
na prakāśyaśca susvapnaḥ paṇḍitaiḥ kāśyape vraja .. 13 ..
4.77.d:
निद्रायां लभते शोकं पण़डिते वाञ्छितं फलम् ।
न प्रकाश्यश्च सुस्वप्नः पण्डितैः काश्यपे व्रज ॥ 13 ॥
4.77.m:
[told] in sleep, he gets sorrow; to a wise person, he attains the desired fruit.
A good dream should not be revealed by wise men, O lord of Vraja, to a Kāśyapa. 13.

4.77.s:
gavāṃ ca kuñjarāṇāṃ ca hayānāṃ ca vrajeśvara .
prāsādānāṃ ca śailānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ ca tathaiva ca .. 14 ..
4.77.d:
गवां च कुञ्जराणां च हयानां च व्रजेश्वर ।
प्रासादानां च शैलानां वृक्षाणां च तथैव च ॥ 14 ॥
4.77.m:
Of cows, elephants, and horses, O lord of Vraja,
as well as of palaces, mountains, and trees— 14.

4.77.s:
ārohaṇaṃ ca dhanadaṃ bhojanaṃ rodanaṃ tathā .
pratigṛhyatathā vīṇāṃ sasyāḍhyāṃ bhūmimālabhet .. 15 ..
4.77.d:
आरोहणं च धनदं भोजनं रोदनं तथा ।
प्रतिगृह्यतथा वीणां सस्याढ्यां भूमिमालभेत् ॥ 15 ॥
4.77.m:
climbing [them] brings wealth, as do eating and weeping;
likewise, having accepted a lute, one obtains land rich with crops. 15.

4.77.s:
śastrāstreṇa yadā viddho vraṇena kṛmiṇā tathā .
viṣṭhayā rudhireṇaiva saṃyukto'pyarthavānbhavet .. 16 ..
4.77.d:
शस्त्रास्त्रेण यदा विद्धो व्रणेन कृमिणा तथा ।
विष्ठया रुधिरेणैव संयुक्तोऽप्यर्थवान्भवेत् ॥ 16 ॥
4.77.m:
When pierced by weapons, or by wounds or worms,
even covered with feces and blood, one becomes wealthy. 16.

4.77.s:
svapne'pyagamyāgamato bhāryālābhaṃ karoti yaḥ .
mūtrasiktaḥ pibecchukaṃ narakaṃ ca viśatyapi .. 17 ..
4.77.d:
स्वप्नेऽप्यगम्यागमतो भार्यालाभं करोति यः ।
मूत्रसिक्तः पिबेच्छुकं नरकं च विशत्यपि ॥ 17 ॥
4.77.m:
He who in a dream secures a wife through incestuous intercourse,
or drenched in urine drinks semen, enters hell. 17.

4.77.s:
nagaraṃ praviśedraktaṃ samudraṃ vā sudhāṃ pibet .
śubhavārtāmavāpnoti vipulaṃ cārthamālabhet .. 18 ..
4.77.d:
नगरं प्रविशेद्रक्तं समुद्रं वा सुधां पिबेत् ।
शुभवार्तामवाप्नोति विपुलं चार्थमालभेत् ॥ 18 ॥
4.77.m:
If one enters a city, or blood, or the ocean, or drinks nectar,
one receives good news and obtains extensive wealth. 18.

4.77.s:
gajaṃ nṛpaṃ suvarṇa ca vṛṣabhaṃ ghenumeva ca .
dīpamannaṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ kanyāṃ chatraṃ rathaṃ dhvajam .. 19 ..
4.77.d:
गजं नृपं सुवर्ण च वृषभं घेनुमेव च ।
दीपमन्नं फलं पुष्पं कन्यां छत्रं रथं ध्वजम् ॥ 19 ॥
4.77.m:
An elephant, a king, gold, a bull, and a cow,
a lamp, food, fruit, a flower, a maiden, an umbrella, a chariot, a banner— 19.

4.77.s:
kuṭumbaṃ labhate dṛṣṭvā kīrtiṃ ca vipulāṃ śriyam .
pūrṇakumbhaṃdvijaṃ vahniṃ puṣpatāmbūlamandiram .. 20 ..
4.77.d:
कुटुम्बं लभते दृष्ट्वा कीर्तिं च विपुलां श्रियम् ।
पूर्णकुम्भंद्विजं वह्निं पुष्पताम्बूलमन्दिरम् ॥ 20 ॥
4.77.m:
seeing [these], one gains a family, fame, and abundant fortune;
a full jar, a twice-born, fire, a flower, betel, a temple, 20.

4.77.s:
śukladhānyaṃ nadaṃ veśyāṃ dṛṣṭvā śriyamavāpnuyāt .
gokṣīraṃ ca ghṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā cārtha puṇyadhanaṃ labhet .. 21 ..
4.77.d:
शुक्लधान्यं नदं वेश्यां दृष्ट्वा श्रियमवाप्नुयात् ।
गोक्षीरं च घृतं दृष्ट्वा चार्थ पुण्यधनं लभेत् ॥ 21 ॥
4.77.m:
white grain, a river, and a courtesan—having seen these, one attains fortune.
Having seen cow's milk and ghee, one attains wealth and virtuous gains. 21.

4.77.s:
pāyasaṃ padmapatre ca dadhi dugdhaṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu .
miṣṭānnaṃ svastikaṃ bhuktvā dhruvaṃ rājā bhaviṣyati .. 22 ..
4.77.d:
पायसं पद्मपत्रे च दधि दुग्धं घृतं मधु ।
मिष्टान्नं स्वस्तिकं भुक्त्वा ध्रुवं राजा भविष्यति ॥ 22 ॥
4.77.m:
Having eaten milk-rice on a lotus leaf, curds, milk, ghee, honey,
sweetmeats, or a svastika sweet, one will certainly become a king. 22.

4.77.s:
pakṣiṇāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca bhuṅkte māṃsaṃ naro yadi .
bahvarthaṃ śubhavārtāṃ ca labhate vāñchitaṃ phalam .. 23 ..
4.77.d:
पक्षिणां मानुषाणां च भुङ्क्ते मांसं नरो यदि ।
बह्वर्थं शुभवार्तां च लभते वाञ्छितं फलम् ॥ 23 ॥
4.77.m:
If a man eats the flesh of birds or humans,
he obtains great wealth, good news, and the desired fruit. 23.

4.77.s:
chatraṃ vā pādukāṃ vā'pi labdhvā dhānyaṃ ca gacchati .
asiṃ ca nirmaraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tattathaiva bhaviṣyati .. 24 ..
4.77.d:
छत्रं वा पादुकां वाऽपि लब्ध्वा धान्यं च गच्छति ।
असिं च निर्मरं तीक्ष्णं तत्तथैव भविष्यति ॥ 24 ॥
4.77.m:
Having obtained an umbrella, shoes, or grain, if he goes away,
or a spotless, sharp sword, the result will be just the same. 24.

4.77.s:
helayā saṃtaredyo hi sa pradhāno bhaviṣyati .
dṛṣṭvā ca phalitaṃ vṛkṣaṃ dhanamāpnoti niścitam .. 25 ..
4.77.d:
हेलया संतरेद्यो हि स प्रधानो भविष्यति ।
दृष्ट्वा च फलितं वृक्षं धनमाप्नोति निश्चितम् ॥ 25 ॥
4.77.m:
He who crosses over [water] with ease will become a chief;
and having seen a tree laden with fruit, he definitely gains wealth. 25.

4.77.s:
sarpeṇa bhakṣito yo hi ṇarthalātraśca tadbhavet .
svapne sūrya vidhuṃ dṛṣṭvā mucyate vyādhibandhanāt .. 26 ..
4.77.d:
सर्पेण भक्षितो यो हि णर्थलात्रश्च तद्भवेत् ।
स्वप्ने सूर्य विधुं दृष्ट्वा मुच्यते व्याधिबन्धनात् ॥ 26 ॥
4.77.m:
One who is eaten by a snake attains wealth on that account.
Seeing the sun or the moon in a dream, one is released from bondage to disease. 26.

4.77.s:
vaḍavāṃ kukkuṭīṃ dṛṣṭvā kauñcīṃ bhāryaṃ labheddhruvam .
svapneyo nigaḍairbaddhaḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ putramālabhet .. 27 ..
4.77.d:
वडवां कुक्कुटीं दृष्ट्वा कौञ्चीं भार्यं लभेद्ध्रुवम् ।
स्वप्नेयो निगडैर्बद्धः प्रतिष्ठां पुत्रमालभेत् ॥ 27 ॥
4.77.m:
Having seen a mare, a hen, or a curlew bird, one surely gets a wife;
he who is bound with fetters in a dream gains status and a son. 27.

4.77.s:
dadhyannaṃ pāyasaṃ bhuṅkate padmapatre nadītaṭe .
viśīrṇapadmapatre ca so'pi rājā maviṣyati .. 28 ..
4.77.d:
दध्यन्नं पायसं भुङ्कते पद्मपत्रे नदीतटे ।
विशीर्णपद्मपत्रे च सोऽपि राजा मविष्यति ॥ 28 ॥
4.77.m:
He who eats curd-rice or milk-rice on a lotus leaf on a riverbank,
or even on a withered lotus leaf, will become a king. 28.

4.77.s:
jalaukasaṃ vṛścikaṃ ca sarpa ca yadi paśyati .
dhanaṃ putraṃ ca vijayaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ vā labhediti .. 29 ..
4.77.d:
जलौकसं वृश्चिकं च सर्प च यदि पश्यति ।
धनं पुत्रं च विजयं प्रतिष्ठां वा लभेदिति ॥ 29 ॥
4.77.m:
If one sees a leech, a scorpion, or a snake,
one attains wealth, a son, victory, or high standing. 29.

4.77.s:
śṛṅgibhirdaṃṣṭribhiḥ kolairvānaraiḥ pīḍito yadi .
niścitaṃ ca bhavedrājā dhanaṃ ca vipulaṃ labhet .. 30 ..
4.77.d:
शृङ्गिभिर्दंष्ट्रिभिः कोलैर्वानरैः पीडितो यदि ।
निश्चितं च भवेद्राजा धनं च विपुलं लभेत् ॥ 30 ॥
4.77.m:
If one is troubled by horned beasts, tusked animals, boars, or monkeys,
he will certainly become a king and acquire abundant wealth. 30.

4.77.s:
matsyaṃ māṃsaṃ mauktikaṃ ca śaṅkhaṃ candanahīrakam .
yastu paśyati svapnānte vipulaṃ dhanamālabhet .. 31 ..
4.77.d:
मत्स्यं मांसं मौक्तिकं च शङ्खं चन्दनहीरकम् ।
यस्तु पश्यति स्वप्नान्ते विपुलं धनमालभेत् ॥ 31 ॥
4.77.m:
He who at the end of a dream sees fish, meat, pearls,
a conch shell, sandalwood, or a diamond, gains vast wealth. 31.

4.77.s:
surāṃ ca rudhiraṃ svarṇa bhuktvā viṣṭhāṃdhanaṃ labhet.
pratimāṃ śivaliṅgaṃca labheddṛṣṭvā jayaṃ dhanam .. 32 ..
4.77.d:
सुरां च रुधिरं स्वर्ण भुक्त्वा विष्ठांधनं लभेत्।
प्रतिमां शिवलिङ्गंच लभेद्दृष्ट्वा जयं धनम् ॥ 32 ॥
4.77.m:
Having consumed liquor, blood, gold, or feces, one obtains wealth.
Having seen an icon or a Śiva-liṅga, one attains victory and wealth. 32.

4.77.s:
phalitaṃ puṣpitaṃ bilvamāmraṃ dṛṣṭvā labheddhanam .
dṛṣṭvā ca jvaladagniṃ ca dhanaṃ buddhiṃ śriyaṃ labhet .. 33 ..
4.77.d:
फलितं पुष्पितं बिल्वमाम्रं दृष्ट्वा लभेद्धनम् ।
दृष्ट्वा च ज्वलदग्निं च धनं बुद्धिं श्रियं लभेत् ॥ 33 ॥
4.77.m:
Having seen a bilva or mango tree blooming and bearing fruit, one gets wealth;
and having seen a blazing fire, one attains wealth, wisdom, and fortune. 33.

4.77.s:
āmalakaṃ dhātrauphalamutpalaṃ ca dhanāgamam .
devatāśca dvijā gāvaḥ pitaro liṅginastathā .. 34 ..
4.77.d:
आमलकं धात्रौफलमुत्पलं च धनागमम् ।
देवताश्च द्विजा गावः पितरो लिङ्गिनस्तथा ॥ 34 ॥
4.77.m:
An āmalaka fruit, an emblic myrobalan, or a blue lotus brings an influx of wealth.
Whatever deities, twice-born, cows, ancestors, and ascetics 34.

4.77.s:
yaddadāti mithaḥsvapne tattathaiva bhaviṣyati .
śuklāmbaradharā nāryaḥ śuklamālyānulepanā .
samāśliṣyanti yaṃ svapne tasya śrīḥ sarvataḥ sukham .. 35 ..
4.77.d:
यद्ददाति मिथःस्वप्ने तत्तथैव भविष्यति ।
शुक्लाम्बरधरा नार्यः शुक्लमाल्यानुलेपना ।
समाश्लिष्यन्ति यं स्वप्ने तस्य श्रीः सर्वतः सुखम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.77.m:
give to one another in a dream, that will come to pass exactly so.
If women clad in white garments, with white garlands and unguents, / embrace someone in a dream, he has fortune and happiness on every side. 35.

4.77.s:
pītāmbaradharāṃ nārīṃ pītamālyānulepanām .
avagūhati yaḥ svapne kalyāṇaṃ tasya jāyate .. 36 ..
4.77.d:
पीताम्बरधरां नारीं पीतमाल्यानुलेपनाम् ।
अवगूहति यः स्वप्ने कल्याणं तस्य जायते ॥ 36 ॥
4.77.m:
He who embraces in a dream a woman clad in yellow garments,
adorned with yellow garlands and unguents, to him auspiciousness occurs. 36.

4.77.s:
sarvāṇi śuklāni praśaṃsitāni bhasmāsthikārpāsavivarjitāni .
sarvāṇi kṛṣṇanyatininditāni gohastivājidvijadevavarjyam .. 37 ..
4.77.d:
सर्वाणि शुक्लानि प्रशंसितानि भस्मास्थिकार्पासविवर्जितानि ।
सर्वाणि कृष्णन्यतिनिन्दितानि गोहस्तिवाजिद्विजदेववर्ज्यम् ॥ 37 ॥
4.77.m:
All white things are praised, except ashes, bones, and cotton;
all black things are deeply censured, except cows, elephants, horses, twice-born, and gods. 37.

4.77.s:
divya strī sasmitā viprā natnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitā .
yasya mandiramāyāti sa priyaṃ labhate dhruvam .. 38 ..
4.77.d:
दिव्य स्त्री सस्मिता विप्रा नत्नभूषणभूषिता ।
यस्य मन्दिरमायाति स प्रियं लभते ध्रुवम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.77.m:
A celestial woman, smiling, twice-born, adorned with jewel ornaments—
into whose house she enters, he surely obtains what is dear. 38.

4.77.s:
svapne ca brahmaṇo devo brāhmaṇī devakanyakā .
brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇī vā'pi saṃtuṣṭā sasmitā satī .. 39 ..
4.77.d:
स्वप्ने च ब्रह्मणो देवो ब्राह्मणी देवकन्यका ।
ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणी वाऽपि संतुष्टा सस्मिता सती ॥ 39 ॥
4.77.m:
In a dream, a divine man of the Brahman, a god, a Brahmin woman, a daughter of the gods,
or a Brahmin or Brahmin woman, pleased, smiling, and chaste, 39.

4.77.s:
phalaṃ dadāti yasmai ca tasya putro bhaviṣyati .
yaṃ svapne brāhmaṇā nanda kurvanti ca śubhāśiṣam .. 40 ..
4.77.d:
फलं ददाति यस्मै च तस्य पुत्रो भविष्यति ।
यं स्वप्ने ब्राह्मणा नन्द कुर्वन्ति च शुभाशिषम् ॥ 40 ॥
4.77.m:
gives fruit to whomever, he will have a son.
To whomsoever Brahmins give an auspicious blessing in a dream, O Nanda... 40.

4.77.s:
yadvadanti bhavettasya tasyaiśvarya bhaveddhruvam .
parituṣṭo dvijaśreṣṭhaśṭā''yāti yasya mandiram .. 41 ..
4.77.d:
यद्वदन्ति भवेत्तस्य तस्यैश्वर्य भवेद्ध्रुवम् ।
परितुष्टो द्विजश्रेष्ठश्टा'ऽयाति यस्य मन्दिरम् ॥ 41 ॥
4.77.m: Whatever they say will happen to him; his sovereign power will surely come to be. / The best of the twice-born, highly pleased, comes to someone's dwelling,

4.77.s:
nārāyaṇaḥ śivo brahmā praviśettu tadāśramam .
saṃpattisvasya bhavati yaśaśca vipulaṃ śubham .. 42 ..
4.77.d:
नारायणः शिवो ब्रह्मा प्रविशेत्तु तदाश्रमम् ।
संपत्तिस्वस्य भवति यशश्च विपुलं शुभम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.77.m: Or Nārāyaṇa, Śiva, or Brahmā enters his hermitage: / wealth belongs to him, along with vast and auspicious fame.

4.77.s:
pade pade sukhaṃ tasya samānaṃ gauravaṃ labhet .
akasmādapi svapne tu labhate surabhiṃ yadi .. 43 ..
4.77.d:
पदे पदे सुखं तस्य समानं गौरवं लभेत् ।
अकस्मादपि स्वप्ने तु लभते सुरभिं यदि ॥ 43 ॥
4.77.m: At every step he finds happiness and attains peerless honour. / If, unexpectedly, he obtains the wish-granting cow Surabhi in a dream,

4.77.s:
bhūmilābho bhavettasya bhāryā cāpi pativratā .
kareṇa kṛtvā hastī yaṃ mastake sthāpayedyadi .. 44 ..
4.77.d:
भूमिलाभो भवेत्तस्य भार्या चापि पतिव्रता ।
करेण कृत्वा हस्ती यं मस्तके स्थापयेद्यदि ॥ 44 ॥
4.77.m: He will acquire land and also a devoted wife. / If an elephant, raising someone with its trunk, places him on its head,

4.77.s:
rājyalābhobhavettasya niścitaṃ ca śrutau matam .
svapne tu brāhmaṇastuṣṭaḥ samāśliṣyatiyaṃ vraja .. 45 ..
4.77.d:
राज्यलाभोभवेत्तस्य निश्चितं च श्रुतौ मतम् ।
स्वप्ने तु ब्राह्मणस्तुष्टः समाश्लिष्यतियं व्रज ॥ 45 ॥
4.77.m: He will acquire a kingdom; this is the definitive opinion in the Veda. / But if in a dream a delighted brāhmaṇa embraces someone, O Vraja,

4.77.s:
tīrthasnāyī bhavetso'pi niścitaṃ ca śriyā'nvitaḥ .
svapne dadāti puṣpaṃ ca yasmai puṇyavate dvijaḥ .. 46 ..
4.77.d:
तीर्थस्नायी भवेत्सोऽपि निश्चितं च श्रियाऽन्वितः ।
स्वप्ने ददाति पुष्पं च यस्मै पुण्यवते द्विजः ॥ 46 ॥
4.77.m: He will become one who bathes in sacred fords and will certainly be endowed with fortune. / If in a dream a twice-born man gives a flower to a virtuous person,

4.77.s:
jayayukto bhavetso'pi yaśasvī ca dharī sukhī .
svapne dṛṣṭavā ca tīrthāni saudharatnagṛhāṇi ca .. 47 ..
4.77.d:
जययुक्तो भवेत्सोऽपि यशस्वी च धरी सुखी ।
स्वप्ने दृष्टवा च तीर्थानि सौधरत्नगृहाणि च ॥ 47 ॥
4.77.m: He will be endowed with victory, renowned, wealthy, and happy. / Having seen sacred fords in a dream, or mansions and jewel-built palaces,

4.77.s:
jayayuktaśca dhanavāṃstīrthasnāyī bhavennaraḥ .
svapne tu pūṇaṃkalaśaṃ kaścitkasmai dadāti ca .. 48 ..
4.77.d:
जययुक्तश्च धनवांस्तीर्थस्नायी भवेन्नरः ।
स्वप्ने तु पूणंकलशं कश्चित्कस्मै ददाति च ॥ 48 ॥
4.77.m: A man will be victorious, wealthy, and one who bathes in sacred fords. / If in a dream someone gives a full jar to a person,

4.77.s:
putralābho bhavettasya maṃpattiṃ vā samālabhet .
haste kṛtvā tu kuḍavamāḍhakaṃ vārasundarī .. 49 ..
4.77.d:
पुत्रलाभो भवेत्तस्य मंपत्तिं वा समालभेत् ।
हस्ते कृत्वा तु कुडवमाढकं वारसुन्दरी ॥ 49 ॥
4.77.m: He will obtain a son or acquire wealth. / If an apsaras, holding in her hand a dry measure or an āḍhaka measure,

4.77.s:
yasya mandiramāyāti sa lakṣmīṃ labhate dhruvam .
divyā strī yadgṛhaṃ gatvā purīṣaṃ visṛjeddvija .. 50 ..
4.77.d:
यस्य मन्दिरमायाति स लक्ष्मीं लभते ध्रुवम् ।
दिव्या स्त्री यद्गृहं गत्वा पुरीषं विसृजेद्द्विज ॥ 50 ॥
4.77.m: Comes to someone's dwelling, he certainly attains Lakṣmī. / If a celestial woman goes to someone's house and discharges feces, O twice-born,

4.77.s:
arthalābho bhavettasya dāridryaṃ ca prayāti ca .
yasya gehaṃ samāyāti brāhmaṇo bhāryayā saha .. 51 ..
4.77.d:
अर्थलाभो भवेत्तस्य दारिद्र्यं च प्रयाति च ।
यस्य गेहं समायाति ब्राह्मणो भार्यया सह ॥ 51 ॥
4.77.m: He will gain wealth, and his poverty will vanish. / To whose house a brāhmaṇa comes together with his wife,

4.77.s:
pārvatyā saha śaṃbhurvā lakṣmyā nārāyaṇo'thavā .
brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇī vā'pi svapne tasmai pradīyate .. 52 ..
4.77.d:
पार्वत्या सह शंभुर्वा लक्ष्म्या नारायणोऽथवा ।
ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणी वाऽपि स्वप्ने तस्मै प्रदीयते ॥ 52 ॥
4.77.m: Or Śambhu with Pārvatī, or Nārāyaṇa with Lakṣmī, / or in a dream a brāhmaṇa or a brāhmaṇa woman gives him

4.77.s:
dhānyaṃ puṣpāñjaliṃ vā'pi tasya śrīḥ sardatomukhī .
muktāhāraṃ puṣpamālyaṃ candanaṃ ca labhedvraja .. 53 ..
4.77.d:
धान्यं पुष्पाञ्जलिं वाऽपि तस्य श्रीः सर्दतोमुखी ।
मुक्ताहारं पुष्पमाल्यं चन्दनं च लभेद्व्रज ॥ 53 ॥
4.77.m: Grain or a handful of flowers, his fortune faces in every direction. / If he obtains a pearl necklace, a garland of flowers, and sandalwood, O Vraja,

4.77.s:
svāpne dadāti vipraśca tasya śrīḥ sarvao .
gorocanaṃ patākāṃ vā haridrāmikṣudaṇḍakam .. 54 ..
4.77.d:
स्वाप्ने ददाति विप्रश्च तस्य श्रीः सर्वओ ।
गोरोचनं पताकां वा हरिद्रामिक्षुदण्डकम् ॥ 54 ॥
4.77.m: Or a brāhmaṇa gives [them] in a dream, his fortune will be everywhere. / If he obtains in a dream yellow orpiment, a flag, turmeric, a stalk of sugarcane,

4.77.s:
siddhānnaṃ ca labhetsvapne tasya śrīḥ sarvao .
brāhmaṇo brahmāṇī vā'pi dadāti yasya mastake .. 55 ..
4.77.d:
सिद्धान्नं च लभेत्स्वप्ने तस्य श्रीः सर्वओ ।
ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्माणी वाऽपि ददाति यस्य मस्तके ॥ 55 ॥
4.77.m: Or cooked food, his fortune will be everywhere. / If a brāhmaṇa or a brāhmaṇa woman places upon someone's head

4.77.s:
chatraṃ vā śuklavānyaṃ va sa carājā bhaviṣyati .
svapne lathasthaḥ puruṣaḥ śuklamālyānulepanaḥ .. 56 ..
4.77.d:
छत्रं वा शुक्लवान्यं व स चराजा भविष्यति ।
स्वप्ने लथस्थः पुरुषः शुक्लमाल्यानुलेपनः ॥ 56 ॥
4.77.m: A parasol or white grains, he will become a king. / In a dream, a man mounted on a chariot, adorned with white garlands and ointments,

4.77.s:
tatrasthodadhi bhuṅkte ca pāyasaṃ vā lṛpo bhavet .
svapne dadāti vipraśca brāhmaṇī ca sudhāṃdadhi .. 57 ..
4.77.d:
तत्रस्थोदधि भुङ्क्ते च पायसं वा लृपो भवेत् ।
स्वप्ने ददाति विप्रश्च ब्राह्मणी च सुधांदधि ॥ 57 ॥
4.77.m: Seated there, eats curds or milk rice, he will become a king. / If in a dream a brāhmaṇa or a brāhmaṇa woman gives nectar, curds,

4.77.s:
praśastapātraṃ yasmai vā so'pi rājā bhaveddhruvam .
kumārī cāṣṭavarṣīyā ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitā .. 58 ..
4.77.d:
प्रशस्तपात्रं यस्मै वा सोऽपि राजा भवेद्ध्रुवम् ।
कुमारी चाष्टवर्षीया रत्नभूषणभूषिता ॥ 58 ॥
4.77.m: Or an auspicious vessel to someone, he too will surely become a king. / An eight-year-old maiden adorned with jewelled ornaments,

4.77.s:
yasya tuṣṭā bhavetsvapne sa bhavetkavipaṇa़ḍitaḥ .
dadāti pustakaṃ svapne yasmai puṇyavate ca sā .. 59 ..
4.77.d:
यस्य तुष्टा भवेत्स्वप्ने स भवेत्कविपण़डितः ।
ददाति पुस्तकं स्वप्ने यस्मै पुण्यवते च सा ॥ 59 ॥
4.77.m: If she is pleased with someone in a dream, he will become a poet and a scholar. / And if she gives a book in a dream to a virtuous person,

4.77.s:
sa bhavedviśvavikhyātaḥ kavīndraḥ paṇa़ḍiteśvaraḥ .
yaṃ pāṭhayati svapne vā māteva ca sutaṃ yathā .. 60 ..
4.77.d:
स भवेद्विश्वविख्यातः कवीन्द्रः पण़डितेश्वरः ।
यं पाठयति स्वप्ने वा मातेव च सुतं यथा ॥ 60 ॥
4.77.m: He will become world-renowned, a lord of poets, and a sovereign of scholars. / Whomsoever she instructs in a dream as a mother teaches her son,

4.77.s:
sarasvatīsutaḥ so'pi tatparo nāsti paṇḍitaḥ .
brāhmaṇaḥ pāṭhayedyaṃ ca piteva yatnapūrvakam .. 61 ..
4.77.d:
सरस्वतीसुतः सोऽपि तत्परो नास्ति पण्डितः ।
ब्राह्मणः पाठयेद्यं च पितेव यत्नपूर्वकम् ॥ 61 ॥
4.77.m: He is a son of Sarasvatī; there is no scholar greater than he. / Whomever a brāhmaṇa instructs with diligence, just as a father does,

4.77.s:
dadāti pustakaṃ prītyā sa ca satsadṛśo bhavet .
prāpnoti pustakaṃ svapne pathi vā yatra tatra vā .. 62 ..
4.77.d:
ददाति पुस्तकं प्रीत्या स च सत्सदृशो भवेत् ।
प्राप्नोति पुस्तकं स्वप्ने पथि वा यत्र तत्र वा ॥ 62 ॥
4.77.m: And affectionately gives a book, he becomes like the virtuous. / If one obtains a book in a dream, whether on the road or anywhere else,

4.77.s:
sa paṇḍito yaśasvī ca vikhyātaśca mahītale .
svapne yasmai mahāmantraṃ vipro vipre dadāti cet .. 63 ..
4.77.d:
स पण्डितो यशस्वी च विख्यातश्च महीतले ।
स्वप्ने यस्मै महामन्त्रं विप्रो विप्रे ददाति चेत् ॥ 63 ॥
4.77.m: He will be a scholar, renowned, and celebrated on earth. / If in a dream a brāhmaṇa gives the great mantra to another brāhmaṇa,

4.77.s:
sa bhavetpuruṣaḥ prājño dhanavānguṇavānsudhīḥ .
svapne dadāti mantraṃ vā pratimāṃ vā śilāmayīm .. 64 ..
4.77.d:
स भवेत्पुरुषः प्राज्ञो धनवान्गुणवान्सुधीः ।
स्वप्ने ददाति मन्त्रं वा प्रतिमां वा शिलामयीम् ॥ 64 ॥
4.77.m: That man will become wise, wealthy, virtuous, and intelligent. / If in a dream he gives a mantra or an image made of stone,

4.77.s:
yasmai dadāti vipraśca mant siddhiśca tadbhavet .
vipraṃ viprasamūhaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā natvā''śiṣaṃ labhet .. 65 ..
4.77.d:
यस्मै ददाति विप्रश्च मन्त् सिद्धिश्च तद्भवेत् ।
विप्रं विप्रसमूहं च दृष्ट्वा नत्वा'ऽशिषं लभेत् ॥ 65 ॥
4.77.m: To whomsoever the brāhmaṇa gives it, attainment of the mantra will be his. / Having seen a brāhmaṇa or a host of brāhmaṇas, having bowed down and received a blessing,

4.77.s:
rājendraḥ sa bhavedvā'pi kiṃvā ca kavipaṇḍitaḥ .
śukladhānyayutāṃ bhūmīṃ yasmai vipra samutsṛjet .. 66 ..
4.77.d:
राजेन्द्रः स भवेद्वाऽपि किंवा च कविपण्डितः ।
शुक्लधान्ययुतां भूमीं यस्मै विप्र समुत्सृजेत् ॥ 66 ॥
4.77.m: He will become an emperor or a poet and scholar. / To whomsoever a brāhmaṇa bestows land filled with white grain,

4.77.s:
svapne'pi parituṣṭaśca sa bhavetpṛthivīpatiḥ .
svapna vipro rathe kṛtvā nānāsvargaṃ pradarśayet .. 67 ..
4.77.d:
स्वप्नेऽपि परितुष्टश्च स भवेत्पृथिवीपतिः ।
स्वप्न विप्रो रथे कृत्वा नानास्वर्गं प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ 67 ॥
4.77.m: Even in a dream, highly pleased, he will become a lord of the earth. / If in a dream a brāhmaṇa places someone on a chariot and shows him various heavens,

4.77.s:
ciraṃjīvī bhavedāyurdhanavṛddhirbhaveddhruvam .
viprāya vipraḥ saṃtuṣṭo yasmai kanyāṃ dadāti ca .. 68 ..
4.77.d:
चिरंजीवी भवेदायुर्धनवृद्धिर्भवेद्ध्रुवम् ।
विप्राय विप्रः संतुष्टो यस्मै कन्यां ददाति च ॥ 68 ॥
4.77.m: He will become long-lived, and his life and wealth will surely increase. / To which brāhmaṇa a gratified brāhmaṇa gives his daughter,

4.77.s:
svapne ca sa bhavennityaṃ dhanāḍhyo bhūvatiḥ svayam .
svapne sarovaraṃ dṛṣṭavā samudraṃ vā nadīṃ nadam .. 69 ..
4.77.d:
स्वप्ने च स भवेन्नित्यं धनाढ्यो भूवतिः स्वयम् ।
स्वप्ने सरोवरं दृष्टवा समुद्रं वा नदीं नदम् ॥ 69 ॥
4.77.m: Even in a dream, he will constantly be rich in wealth and a lord of the earth himself. / Having seen a lake, an ocean, a river, or a stream in a dream,

4.77.s:
śuklāhiṃ śuklaśailaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā śriyamavāpnuyāt .
yaṃ paśyanti mṛtaṃ svapne sa bhaveccirajīvanaḥ .. 70 ..
4.77.d:
शुक्लाहिं शुक्लशैलं च दृष्ट्वा श्रियमवाप्नुयात् ।
यं पश्यन्ति मृतं स्वप्ने स भवेच्चिरजीवनः ॥ 70 ॥
4.77.m: And having seen a white serpent and a white mountain, he will obtain fortune. / Whomsoever they see dead in a dream will have a long life.

4.77.s:
arogī rogiṇaṃ du khī suśinaṃ ca sukhaṃ bhavet .
divyā strī yaṃ pravadati mama svāmī bhavāniti .. 71 ..
4.77.d:
अरोगी रोगिणं दु खी सुशिनं च सुखं भवेत् ।
दिव्या स्त्री यं प्रवदति मम स्वामी भवानिति ॥ 71 ॥
4.77.m: A diseased person will become healthy; a sorrowful person will attain happiness and joy. / To whom a celestial woman says, 'You are my husband,'

4.77.s:
svapne dṛṣṭvā ca cāgatiṃ sa ca rājā bhaveddṛḍham .
svapne vā kālikāṃ dṛṣṭvā labdhavā sphaṭikamālikām .. 72 ..
4.77.d:
स्वप्ने दृष्ट्वा च चागतिं स च राजा भवेद्दृढम् ।
स्वप्ने वा कालिकां दृष्ट्वा लब्धवा स्फटिकमालिकाम् ॥ 72 ॥
4.77.m: Seeing her approach in a dream, he will firmly become a king. / Or having seen Kālī in a dream, or having obtained a rosary of crystal,

4.77.s:
indracāpaṃ śakravajraṃ sa pratiṣṭhāṃ labheddhruvam .
svapne vadati yaṃ vipro mama dāso bhaveti ca .. 73 ..
4.77.d:
इन्द्रचापं शक्रवज्रं स प्रतिष्ठां लभेद्ध्रुवम् ।
स्वप्ने वदति यं विप्रो मम दासो भवेति च ॥ 73 ॥
4.77.m: A rainbow, or the thunderbolt of Indra, he will surely attain high standing. / To whom a brāhmaṇa says in a dream, 'Be my servant,'

4.77.s:
haridāsyaṃ ca madbhaktiṃ sa labdhvā vaiṣṇavo bhavet .
svapne vipro harīḥ śaṃbhurbrāhmaṇī kamalā śivā .. 74 ..
4.77.d:
हरिदास्यं च मद्भक्तिं स लब्ध्वा वैष्णवो भवेत् ।
स्वप्ने विप्रो हरीः शंभुर्ब्राह्मणी कमला शिवा ॥ 74 ॥
4.77.m: He will attain servitude to Hari and devotion to Me, and become a Vaiṣṇava. / In a dream, a brāhmaṇa is Hari or Śambhu; a brāhmaṇa woman is Kamalā or Śivā;

4.77.s:
śaklā strī devamātā vā jāhnavī vā sarasvatī .
gopālikāveṣadharī bālikā rādhikā mama .. 75 ..
4.77.d:
शक्ला स्त्री देवमाता वा जाह्नवी वा सरस्वती ।
गोपालिकावेषधरी बालिका राधिका मम ॥ 75 ॥
4.77.m: A fair woman is the mother of the gods, the Gaṅgā, or Sarasvatī; / a young girl wearing the attire of a cowherd woman is My Rādhikā;

4.77.s:
bālaśca bālagopālaḥ svapnavidbhiḥ prakāśitaḥ .
eṣa te kathito nanda susvapnaḥ puṇyahetukaḥ ..
śrotumicchasi kiṃ vā tvaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ kathayāmi te .. 76 ..
4.77.d:
बालश्च बालगोपालः स्वप्नविद्भिः प्रकाशितः ।
एष ते कथितो नन्द सुस्वप्नः पुण्यहेतुकः ॥
श्रोतुमिच्छसि किं वा त्वं किं भूयः कथयामि ते ॥ 76 ॥
4.77.m:
And a young boy is Bālagopāla—so it has been revealed by those who know dreams. / This auspicious dream caused by religious merit has been told to you, O Nanda;
What do you wish to hear, or what more shall I tell you?

4.77.s:
iti śrībrahmao mahāo śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhao uttao nārādanāo susvapnakathānaṃ
nāma saptasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 77 ..
4.77.d:
इति श्रीब्रह्मओ महाओ श्रीकृष्णजन्मखओ उत्तओ नारादनाओ सुस्वप्नकथानं
नाम सप्तसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः ॥ 77 ॥
4.77.m: Thus ends the seventy-seventh chapter, entitled 'Discourse on Auspicious Dreams', in the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the Śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍa in the great Śrībrahmavaivarta Purāṇa.

4.78.s:
nanda uvāca
śrīqaṣṇa jagatāṃ nātha susvapnaśca śruto mayā .
vedasāro nītisāro laukiko vaidikastathā .. 1 ..
4.78.d:
नन्द उवाच
श्रीqअष्ण जगतां नाथ सुस्वप्नश्च श्रुतो मया ।
वेदसारो नीतिसारो लौकिको वैदिकस्तथा ॥ 1 ॥
4.78.m: Now begins the seventy-eighth chapter. / Nanda said: / O Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Lord of the worlds, the auspicious dream has been heard by me, / which is the essence of the Vedas, the essence of conduct, worldly as well as Vedic.

4.78.s:
adhunā śrotumicchāmi pāpaṃ yeṣāṃ ca darśane .
yasminkarmaṇi vā vatsa tanmāṃ kathitumarhasi .. 2 ..
4.78.d:
अधुना श्रोतुमिच्छामि पापं येषां च दर्शने ।
यस्मिन्कर्मणि वा वत्स तन्मां कथितुमर्हसि ॥ 2 ॥
4.78.m: Now I wish to hear what brings sin upon the sight of it, / or in what action, O child; that you ought to tell me.

4.78.s:
vacanaṃ vedaśāśroktaṃ tathā vedānuyāyinaḥ .
śrotumicchanti saṃtaptā lokāstvanmukhatastathā .. 3 ..
4.78.d:
वचनं वेदशाश्रोक्तं तथा वेदानुयायिनः ।
श्रोतुमिच्छन्ति संतप्ता लोकास्त्वन्मुखतस्तथा ॥ 3 ॥
4.78.m: Afflicted people, followers of the Vedas, likewise desire to hear from Your mouth / words spoken in the Vedic treatises.

4.78.s:
vedānāṃ janakastvaṃ ca vaidikānāṃ satāmapi .
prahmādīnāṃ surāṇāṃ ca munīnāṃ jagatāmapi .. 4 ..
4.78.d:
वेदानां जनकस्त्वं च वैदिकानां सतामपि ।
प्रह्मादीनां सुराणां च मुनीनां जगतामपि ॥ 4 ॥
4.78.m: You are the father of the Vedas, of the followers of the Vedas, of the virtuous, / of the gods led by Brahmā, of the sages, and of all the worlds.

4.78.s:
śrutaṃ yattvanmukhāmbhojātpramāṇaṃ vacanāmṛtam .
tena deho'bhiṣikto me vatsavicchedadāhanaḥ .. 5 ..
4.78.d:
श्रुतं यत्त्वन्मुखाम्भोजात्प्रमाणं वचनामृतम् ।
तेन देहोऽभिषिक्तो मे वत्सविच्छेददाहनः ॥ 5 ॥
4.78.m: The authoritative nectar of words that has been heard from Your lotus mouth / has sprinkled my body, which had been burning with the torment of separation from you, my child.

4.78.s:
svapne yaccharaṇāmbhojaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam .
brahmādayo na paśyanti tadadya dṛṣṭigocaram .. 6 ..
4.78.d:
स्वप्ने यच्छरणाम्भोजं सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ।
ब्रह्मादयो न पश्यन्ति तदद्य दृष्टिगोचरम् ॥ 6 ॥
4.78.m: The lotus feet that even Brahmā and the gods do not see in a dream, / granting the fruit of all desires—those very feet have today come within range of my sight.

4.78.s:
ataḥ paraṃ tvatpadābjaṃ kva paśyāmi ca pātakī .
viṇmūtradhārī deho me nibaddhaśca svakarmaṇā .. 7 ..
4.78.d:
अतः परं त्वत्पदाब्जं क्व पश्यामि च पातकी ।
विण्मूत्रधारी देहो मे निबद्धश्च स्वकर्मणा ॥ 7 ॥
4.78.m: Beyond this, where will I, a sinner, see your lotus feet? / My body carries feces and urine and is bound by its own karma.

4.78.s:
īdṛśaṃ ca dinaṃ vatsa kadā mama bhaviṣyati .
tvayā brahmādināthena saṃvādo mama pāpinaḥ .. 8 ..
4.78.d:
ईदृशं च दिनं वत्स कदा मम भविष्यति ।
त्वया ब्रह्मादिनाथेन संवादो मम पापिनः ॥ 8 ॥
4.78.m: And when will such a day come for me, child, / when I, a sinner, converse with you, the Lord of Brahmā and the others?

4.78.s:
kṛpāṃ kuru kṛpānātha mama doṣaṃ kṣamasva ca .
vatsabuddhyā ca durnītaṃ yatkṛtaṃ ca maheśvara .. 9 ..
4.78.d:
कृपां कुरु कृपानाथ मम दोषं क्षमस्व च ।
वत्सबुद्ध्या च दुर्नीतं यत्कृतं च महेश्वर ॥ 9 ॥
4.78.m: Show mercy, O Lord of mercy, and forgive my fault, / and whatever misconduct was done regarding you as a child, O Maheśvara.

4.78.s:
brahmeśaśeṣamunayo dhyāyante tvatpadāmbujam .
sarasvatī śrutiryasya stavane jaḍatāṃ vrajet .. 10 ..
4.78.d:
ब्रह्मेशशेषमुनयो ध्यायन्ते त्वत्पदाम्बुजम् ।
सरस्वती श्रुतिर्यस्य स्तवने जडतां व्रजेत् ॥ 10 ॥
4.78.m: Brahmā, Īśa, Śeṣa, and the sages meditate on your lotus feet; / Sarasvatī and the Śruti become mute in praising you.

4.78.s:
ityevamuktvā nandaśca nirānandaḥ śucā''kulaḥ .
mūrcchāmāpa ruditvā ca putravicchedavihvalaḥ .. 11 ..
4.78.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा नन्दश्च निरानन्दः शुचा'ऽकुलः ।
मूर्च्छामाप रुदित्वा च पुत्रविच्छेदविह्वलः ॥ 11 ॥
4.78.m: Having spoken thus, Nanda, joyless and overwhelmed with grief, / wept and fell into a swoon, distraught by separation from his son.

4.78.s:
saṃtrasto bhagavānkṛṣṇo bodhayāmāsa yatnataḥ .
paramādhyātmikaṃ jñānaṃ dadau tasmai jagatpatiḥ .. 12 ..
4.78.d:
संत्रस्तो भगवान्कृष्णो बोधयामास यत्नतः ।
परमाध्यात्मिकं ज्ञानं ददौ तस्मै जगत्पतिः ॥ 12 ॥
4.78.m: Alarmed, the Blessed Kṛṣṇa carefully awakened him; / the Lord of the universe gave him the highest spiritual knowledge.

4.78.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
he nanda janakaśreṣṭha sarvaśreṣṭha vrajeśvara .
cetanaṃ kuru kalyāma jñānaṃ ca paramaṃ śrṛṇu .. 13 ..
4.78.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
हे नन्द जनकश्रेष्ठ सर्वश्रेष्ठ व्रजेश्वर ।
चेतनं कुरु कल्याम ज्ञानं च परमं श्रृणु ॥ 13 ॥
4.78.m: The Blessed Lord said: / O Nanda, best of fathers, best of all, lord of Vraja, / regain consciousness, auspicious one, and hear the highest knowledge.

4.78.s:
paramādhyātmikaṃ jñānaṃ jñānināṃ ca sudulrabham .
vedaśāstre gopanīyaṃ tubhyameva dadāmyaham .. 14 ..
4.78.d:
परमाध्यात्मिकं ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनां च सुदुल्रभम् ।
वेदशास्त्रे गोपनीयं तुभ्यमेव ददाम्यहम् ॥ 14 ॥
4.78.m: The highest spiritual knowledge is very difficult even for the wise to attain; / concealed in the Veda and the scriptures, I give it to you alone.

4.78.s:
nibodha śrūyatāṃ nanda sānandaḥ susamāhitaḥ .
janmamṛtyucarāvyādhiryadabhyāsānna jāyate .. 15 ..
4.78.d:
निबोध श्रूयतां नन्द सानन्दः सुसमाहितः ।
जन्ममृत्युचराव्याधिर्यदभ्यासान्न जायते ॥ 15 ॥
4.78.m: Understand, let it be heard, Nanda, joyful and well composed, / that by whose practice birth, death, old age, and disease do not occur.

4.78.s:
sthiro bhava mahārāja vrajanātha vrajaṃ vraja .
jñānaṃ labdhvā sadānandaḥ śokamohavivarjitaḥ .. 16 ..
4.78.d:
स्थिरो भव महाराज व्रजनाथ व्रजं व्रज ।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा सदानन्दः शोकमोहविवर्जितः ॥ 16 ॥
4.78.m: Be steady, great king, lord of Vraja; go to Vraja. / Having attained knowledge, remain always joyful, free from grief and delusion.

4.78.s:
jalabudbudavatsarvaṃ saṃsāraṃ sacarācaram .
prabhāte svapnavanmithyā mohakāraṇameva ca .. 17 ..
4.78.d:
जलबुद्बुदवत्सर्वं संसारं सचराचरम् ।
प्रभाते स्वप्नवन्मिथ्या मोहकारणमेव च ॥ 17 ॥
4.78.m: The whole world, moving and unmoving, is like a water bubble; / at dawn it is false like a dream, the cause of delusion alone.

4.78.s:
mithyākṛtrimanirmāṇahetuśca pāñcabhautikaḥ .
māyayā satyabuddhyā ca pratītiṃ jāyate naraḥ .. 18 ..
4.78.d:
मिथ्याकृत्रिमनिर्माणहेतुश्च पाञ्चभौतिकः ।
मायया सत्यबुद्ध्या च प्रतीतिं जायते नरः ॥ 18 ॥
4.78.m: And its cause is made of the five elements, an unreal, artificial construction; / through māyā, taking it to be real, a man develops conviction [in it].

4.78.s:
kāmakrodharobhamohairveṣṭitaḥ sarvakarmasu .
māyayā mohitaḥ śaśvajjñānahīnaśca durbalaḥ .. 19 ..
4.78.d:
कामक्रोधरोभमोहैर्वेष्टितः सर्वकर्मसु ।
मायया मोहितः शश्वज्ज्ञानहीनश्च दुर्बलः ॥ 19 ॥
4.78.m: Encompassed by desire, anger, greed, and delusion in all actions, / he is constantly bewildered by māyā, lacking knowledge, and weak;

4.78.s:
nidrātandrākṣutpipāsākṣamāśraddhādayādibhiḥ .
lajjā śāntirdhṛtiḥ puṣṭistuṣṭiścā''bhiśca veṣṭitaḥ .. 20 ..
4.78.d:
निद्रातन्द्राक्षुत्पिपासाक्षमाश्रद्धादयादिभिः ।
लज्जा शान्तिर्धृतिः पुष्टिस्तुष्टिश्चा'ऽभिश्च वेष्टितः ॥ 20 ॥
4.78.m: encompassed by sleep, drowsiness, hunger, thirst, forbearance, faith, compassion, and the like, / by shame, tranquility, firmness, nourishment, and contentment;

4.78.s:
manobuddhicetanābhiḥ prāṇajñānātmabhiḥ saha .
saṃsaktaḥ sarvadevaiśca yathā vṛkṣaśca vāyasaiḥ .. 21 ..
4.78.d:
मनोबुद्धिचेतनाभिः प्राणज्ञानात्मभिः सह ।
संसक्तः सर्वदेवैश्च यथा वृक्षश्च वायसैः ॥ 21 ॥
4.78.m: together with mind, intellect, consciousness, vital breaths, knowledge, and self, / clinged to by all the gods, just as a tree by crows.

4.78.s:
ahamātmā ca sarveśaḥ sarvajñānātmakaḥ smṛtaḥ .
mano brahmā ca prakṛtirbuddhirupā sanātanī .. 22 ..
4.78.d:
अहमात्मा च सर्वेशः सर्वज्ञानात्मकः स्मृतः ।
मनो ब्रह्मा च प्रकृतिर्बुद्धिरुपा सनातनी ॥ 22 ॥
4.78.m: I am the Self, the Lord of all, known as the essence of all knowledge. / The mind is Brahmā, and Prakṛti is the eternal form of the intellect.

4.78.s:
prāṇā viṣṇuścetanā sā padmā tu cādhidevatā .
mayi sthite sthitāḥ sarve gatāste'pigate mayi .. 23 ..
4.78.d:
प्राणा विष्णुश्चेतना सा पद्मा तु चाधिदेवता ।
मयि स्थिते स्थिताः सर्वे गतास्तेऽपिगते मयि ॥ 23 ॥
4.78.m: The vital breaths are Viṣṇu, and consciousness is Padmā, the presiding deity. / While I abide, all abide; when I am gone, they too are gone.

4.78.s:
asmābhiśca vinā dehaḥ sadyaḥ patati niścitam .
pāñcabhūto vilīnaśca pañcabhūteṣu tatkṣaṇam .. 24 ..
4.78.d:
अस्माभिश्च विना देहः सद्यः पतति निश्चितम् ।
पाञ्चभूतो विलीनश्च पञ्चभूतेषु तत्क्षणम् ॥ 24 ॥
4.78.m: Without us, the body certainly falls instantly, / and, composed of the five elements, dissolves into the five elements at that very moment.

4.78.s:
nāmasaṃketarūpaṃ ca niṣphalaṃ mohakāraṇam .
śokaścājñānināṃ tāta jñānitāṃ nāsti kiṃcana .. 25 ..
4.78.d:
नामसंकेतरूपं च निष्फलं मोहकारणम् ।
शोकश्चाज्ञानिनां तात ज्ञानितां नास्ति किंचन ॥ 25 ॥
4.78.m: Name and sign-form are fruitless, a cause of delusion; / grief belongs to the ignorant, father; for the wise there is none at all.

4.78.s:
nidrādayaḥ śaktayaśca tāḥ sarvāḥ prakṛte kalāḥ .
lobhādayo hyadharmāśāstathā'haṃkārapañcamaḥ .. 26 ..
4.78.d:
निद्रादयः शक्तयश्च ताः सर्वाः प्रकृते कलाः ।
लोभादयो ह्यधर्माशास्तथाऽहंकारपञ्चमः ॥ 26 ॥
4.78.m: Powers such as sleep are all portions of Prakṛti; / greed and the rest are parts of unrighteousness, with egoism as the fifth.

4.78.s:
te brahmaviṣṇurudrāśā guṇāḥ sattvādayastrayaḥ .
jñānātmakaḥ śivo jyotirahamātmā ca nirguṇaḥ .. 27 ..
4.78.d:
ते ब्रह्मविष्णुरुद्राशा गुणाः सत्त्वादयस्त्रयः ।
ज्ञानात्मकः शिवो ज्योतिरहमात्मा च निर्गुणः ॥ 27 ॥
4.78.m: The three gunas, beginning with sattva, are portions of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra; / Śiva consists of knowledge, light, and I am the Self, beyond the gunas.

4.78.s:
yadā viśāmi prakṛtau tadā'haṃ saguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ .
saguṇā viṣayā viṣṇuprahmarudrādayastathā .. 28 ..
4.78.d:
यदा विशामि प्रकृतौ तदाऽहं सगुणः स्मृतः ।
सगुणा विषया विष्णुप्रह्मरुद्रादयस्तथा ॥ 28 ॥
4.78.m: When I enter into Prakṛti, then I am considered to have form; / with gunas are the objects of sense, and likewise Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Rudra, and the rest.

4.78.s:
dharmo madaṃśo viṣayī śoṣaḥ sūryaḥ kalānidhiḥ .
evaṃ sarve satkalāṃśā munimanvādayaḥsurāḥ .. 29 ..
4.78.d:
धर्मो मदंशो विषयी शोषः सूर्यः कलानिधिः ।
एवं सर्वे सत्कलांशा मुनिमन्वादयःसुराः ॥ 29 ॥
4.78.m: Dharma is a portion of me, sense-enjoying Śeṣa, the Sun, and the Moon; / thus all sages, Manus, and gods are portions of my good parts.

4.78.s:
sarvadehe praviṣṭo'haṃ na liptaḥ sarvakarmasu .
jīvanmuktaśca madbhakto janmamṛtyujarāharaḥ .. 30 ..
4.78.d:
सर्वदेहे प्रविष्टोऽहं न लिप्तः सर्वकर्मसु ।
जीवन्मुक्तश्च मद्भक्तो जन्ममृत्युजराहरः ॥ 30 ॥
4.78.m: I have entered into all bodies, yet I am untainted by all actions; / my devotee is liberated while living, a destroyer of birth, death, and old age.

4.78.s:
sarvasiddheśvaraḥ śrīmānkīrtimānpaṇa़ḍitaḥ kaviḥ .
caturstriśadvidhaḥ siddhaḥ sarvakarmopahārakaḥ .. 31 ..
4.78.d:
सर्वसिद्धेश्वरः श्रीमान्कीर्तिमान्पण़डितः कविः ।
चतुर्स्त्रिशद्विधः सिद्धः सर्वकर्मोपहारकः ॥ 31 ॥
4.78.m: He is the master of all perfections, glorious, renowned, learned, and a sage; / he has the thirty-four kinds of perfection, an offering-maker of all deeds.

4.78.s:
tamupaimi svayaṃ siddhaṃ bhaktastvanyanna vāñchati .
dvāviṃśatividhaṃ siddhaṃ siddhisādhanakāraṇam .. 32 ..
4.78.d:
तमुपैमि स्वयं सिद्धं भक्तस्त्वन्यन्न वाञ्छति ।
द्वाविंशतिविधं सिद्धं सिद्धिसाधनकारणम् ॥ 32 ॥
4.78.m: I myself come to that perfected one; the devotee desires nothing else. / The cause of accomplishing perfections has twenty-two perfections.

4.78.s:
manmukhācchūyatāṃ nanda siddhamantraṃ gṛhāṇa ca .
aṇimā laghimā prāptiḥ prākāmyaṃ mahimā tathā .. 33 ..
4.78.d:
मन्मुखाच्छूयतां नन्द सिद्धमन्त्रं गृहाण च ।
अणिमा लघिमा प्राप्तिः प्राकाम्यं महिमा तथा ॥ 33 ॥
4.78.m: Let it be heard from my mouth, Nanda, and receive the perfected mantra: / miniaturization, lightness, reach, irresistible will, and greatness;

4.78.s:
īśitvaṃ ca vaśitvaṃ ca tathā kāmāvasāyitā .
dūraśravaṇameveti parakāyapraveśanam .. 34 ..
4.78.d:
ईशित्वं च वशित्वं च तथा कामावसायिता ।
दूरश्रवणमेवेति परकायप्रवेशनम् ॥ 34 ॥
4.78.m: mastery, subjugation, and fulfillment of desires; / hearing from afar, entering another's body,

4.78.s:
manoyāyitvameveti sarvajñatvamabhīpsitam .
vahnistambhaṃ jalastambhaṃ ciraṃjīvitvameva ca .. 35 ..
4.78.d:
मनोयायित्वमेवेति सर्वज्ञत्वमभीप्सितम् ।
वह्निस्तम्भं जलस्तम्भं चिरंजीवित्वमेव च ॥ 35 ॥
4.78.m: moving at the speed of thought, the desired omniscience, / arresting fire, arresting water, and long life,

4.78.s:
vāyustambhaṃ kṣutpipāsānidrāstambhanameva ca .
kāyavyūhaṃ ca vāksiddhiṃ mṛtānayanamaupsitam .. 36 ..
4.78.d:
वायुस्तम्भं क्षुत्पिपासानिद्रास्तम्भनमेव च ।
कायव्यूहं च वाक्सिद्धिं मृतानयनमौप्सितम् ॥ 36 ॥
4.78.m: arresting wind, arresting hunger, thirst, and sleep, / multiplying the body, perfection of speech, the desired bringing back of the dead,

4.78.s:
sṛṣṭīnāṃ karaṇaṃ caiva prāṇākarṣaṇameva ca .
oṃ sarveśvareśvarāya sarvadighnavināśine madhusūdanāya svāheti .. 37 ..
4.78.d:
सृष्टीनां करणं चैव प्राणाकर्षणमेव च ।
ओं सर्वेश्वरेश्वराय सर्वदिघ्नविनाशिने मधुसूदनाय स्वाहेति ॥ 37 ॥
4.78.m: the performing of creations, and the drawing forth of the vital breath: / 'Oṃ, svāhā to the Lord of all lords, the destroyer of all obstacles, to Madhusūdana.'

4.78.s:
ayaṃ santro mahāgūḍhaḥ sarveṣāṃ kalpapādapaḥ .
sāmavede ca kathitaḥ middhānāṃ sarvamiddhidaḥ .. 38 ..
4.78.d:
अयं सन्त्रो महागूढः सर्वेषां कल्पपादपः ।
सामवेदे च कथितः मिद्धानां सर्वमिद्धिदः ॥ 38 ॥
4.78.m: This mantra is deeply secret, a wish-fulfilling tree for all; / spoken in the Sāmaveda, it gives all perfections to the perfected.

4.78.s:
anena yoginaḥ siddhā munīndrāśca surāstathā .
śatalakṣajapenaiva mantrasiddhirbhavetsatām .. 39 ..
4.78.d:
अनेन योगिनः सिद्धा मुनीन्द्राश्च सुरास्तथा ।
शतलक्षजपेनैव मन्त्रसिद्धिर्भवेत्सताम् ॥ 39 ॥
4.78.m: By this, yogins, lords of sages, and the gods became perfected; / only by reciting it ten million times does the perfection of the mantra occur for the virtuous.

4.78.s:
yadi nārāyaṇakṣetre haviṣyānnarato japet .
gatvā kuru japaṃ tātakāśikāṃ maṇikarṇikām .. 40 ..
4.78.d:
यदि नारायणक्षेत्रे हविष्यान्नरतो जपेत् ।
गत्वा कुरु जपं तातकाशिकां मणिकर्णिकाम् ॥ 40 ॥
4.78.m: If one devoted to sacrificial food recites it in a sacred site of Nārāyaṇa— / go, father, and perform recitation at Maṇikarṇikā in Kāśī.

4.78.s:
śrṛśu nārāyaṇakṣetrai jalādhastaccatuṣṭayam .
atra nārāyaṇaḥ svāmī nānyaḥ svāmī kadācana .. 41 ..
4.78.d:
श्रृशु नारायणक्षेत्रै जलाधस्तच्चतुष्टयम् ।
अत्र नारायणः स्वामी नान्यः स्वामी कदाचन ॥ 41 ॥
4.78.m: Hear the four sacred sites of Nārāyaṇa under water; / here Nārāyaṇa is the master, no other is ever master.

4.78.s:
jñānaṃ cātra mṛte loke mūrtirbhavati tasya vai .
vrataṃ vinā'pi mantreṇa jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ .. 42 ..
4.78.d:
ज्ञानं चात्र मृते लोके मूर्तिर्भवति तस्य वै ।
व्रतं विनाऽपि मन्त्रेण जीवन्मुक्तो न संशयः ॥ 42 ॥
4.78.m: And there, when a person dies, he attains knowledge and becomes an image of him; / even without a vow, through the mantra he is liberated while living, no doubt.

4.78.s:
vrajaṃ kuru pavitraṃ ca vrajanātha vrajaṃ vraja .
pāpaṃ yaddarśane tāta kathayāmi niśāmaya .. 43 ..
4.78.d:
व्रजं कुरु पवित्रं च व्रजनाथ व्रजं व्रज ।
पापं यद्दर्शने तात कथयामि निशामय ॥ 43 ॥
4.78.m: Make Vraja pure, lord of Vraja; go to Vraja. / The sin incurred by seeing whom, father, I shall declare; listen:

4.78.s:
duḥsvapnaṃ pāpabaujaṃ ca kevalaṃ vighnakāraṇam .
goghnaṃ ca brāhmaṇaghnaṃ vā kṛtaghnaṃ kṛṭilaṃ tathā .. 44 ..
4.78.d:
दुःस्वप्नं पापबौजं च केवलं विघ्नकारणम् ।
गोघ्नं च ब्राह्मणघ्नं वा कृतघ्नं कृटिलं तथा ॥ 44 ॥
4.78.m: a bad dream, a seed of sin, purely a cause of obstacles; / a killer of cows, a killer of brahmins, an ungrateful person, and a deceitful one;

4.78.s:
devaghnaṃ pitṛmātṛghnaṃ pāpaṃ viśvavāsaghātinam .
mithyāsākṣipradātāraṃ yaṃ cā''tithyavivañcanam .. 45 ..
4.78.d:
देवघ्नं पितृमातृघ्नं पापं विश्ववासघातिनम् ।
मिथ्यासाक्षिप्रदातारं यं चा'ऽतिथ्यविवञ्चनम् ॥ 45 ॥
4.78.m: a killer of gods, a killer of parents, the sinful betrayer of trust, / a giver of false witness, and one who denies hospitality;

4.78.s:
grāmayājinameveti devaviprasvahāriṇam .
aśvatthaghātinaṃ duṣṭaṃ śivaviṣṇuvinindakam .. 46 ..
4.78.d:
ग्रामयाजिनमेवेति देवविप्रस्वहारिणम् ।
अश्वत्थघातिनं दुष्टं शिवविष्णुविनिन्दकम् ॥ 46 ॥
4.78.m: a village-priest, a stealer of property of gods and brahmins, / a destroyer of an aśvattha tree, an evil person, a reviler of Śiva and Viṣṇu;

4.78.s:
adīkṣitamanācāraṃ saṃdhyāhīnaṃ dvijaṃ tathā .
devalaṃ vṛṣavāhaṃ ca śūdrāṇāṃ sūpakārakam .. 47 ..
4.78.d:
अदीक्षितमनाचारं संध्याहीनं द्विजं तथा ।
देवलं वृषवाहं च शूद्राणां सूपकारकम् ॥ 47 ॥
4.78.m: one uninitiated, ill-behaved, a twice-born lacking twilight prayers, / a professional temple-priest, a bullock-driver, a cook for Śūdras;

4.78.s:
śavadāhaṃ ca śūdrāṇāṃ śūdraśrāddhānnabhojinam .
avīrāṃ chinnanāsāṃ ca devabrāhmaṇanindakām .. 48 ..
4.78.d:
शवदाहं च शूद्राणां शूद्रश्राद्धान्नभोजिनम् ।
अवीरां छिन्ननासां च देवब्राह्मणनिन्दकाम् ॥ 48 ॥
4.78.m: a burner of Śūdras' corpses, an eater of Śūdras' funeral feast, / a woman without husband or son, a woman whose nose is cut off, a reviler of gods and brahmins;

4.78.s:
padibhaktiviṅīnāṃ ca viṣṇubhaktivihīnakām .
śūdrāṇāṃ vidhavāṃ caiva cāṇḍālīṃ vyabhicāriṇīm .. 49 ..
4.78.d:
पदिभक्तिविङीनां च विष्णुभक्तिविहीनकाम् ।
शूद्राणां विधवां चैव चाण्डालीं व्यभिचारिणीम् ॥ 49 ॥
4.78.m: a woman lacking devotion to her husband, one lacking devotion to Viṣṇu, / a widow of Śūdras, an outcaste woman, an adulteress;

4.78.s:
śaśvatkopayutaṃ duṣṭamṛṇagrastaṃ ca jārajam .
cauraṃ mithyāvādinaṃ ca śaraṇāgatayāyinam .. 50 ..
4.78.d:
शश्वत्कोपयुतं दुष्टमृणग्रस्तं च जारजम् ।
चौरं मिथ्यावादिनं च शरणागतयायिनम् ॥ 50 ॥
4.78.m: one constantly full of anger, wicked, indebted, born of adultery, / a thief, a liar, and one who flees from a suppliant.

4.78.s:
māṃsāpahāriṇaṃ caiva brahmaṇaṃ vṛṣalīpatim .
brāhmaṇīgāmiraṃ śūdra dvijaṃ vādhurṣikaṃ tathā .. 51 ..
4.78.d:
मांसापहारिणं चैव ब्रह्मणं वृषलीपतिम् ।
ब्राह्मणीगामिरं शूद्र द्विजं वाधुर्षिकं तथा ॥ 51 ॥
4.78.m: And a meat-thief, a Brahmin who is the husband of a Śūdra woman, / a Śūdra who has intercourse with a Brahmin woman, and likewise an usurious twice-born; // 51

4.78.s:
agamyāmāminaṃ duṣṭaṃ caturvaṇaṃ narādhamam .
mātā sapatnīmātā ca śvaśrūśca bhaginī sutā .. 52 ..
4.78.d:
अगम्यामामिनं दुष्टं चतुर्वणं नराधमम् ।
माता सपत्नीमाता च श्वश्रूश्च भगिनी सुता ॥ 52 ॥
4.78.m: one who has intercourse with forbidden women, a wicked man, the lowest of men among the four classes. / Mother, step-mother, mother-in-law, sister, daughter, // 52

4.78.s:
gurupatnī putrapatnī sodarasya priyā satī .
mātṛṣvasā pitṛṣvasā bhāmineyapriyā tathā .. 53 ..
4.78.d:
गुरुपत्नी पुत्रपत्नी सोदरस्य प्रिया सती ।
मातृष्वसा पितृष्वसा भामिनेयप्रिया तथा ॥ 53 ॥
4.78.m: guru's wife, son's wife, virtuous beloved wife of a brother, / mother's sister, father's sister, and likewise a sister's son's beloved [wife], // 53

4.78.s:
mātulānī navoḍhā ya pitṛvyastrī rajasvalā .
pitṛmātṛprasūścaiva cāgamyāṣṭādaśa smṛtāḥ .. 54 ..
4.78.d:
मातुलानी नवोढा य पितृव्यस्त्री रजस्वला ।
पितृमातृप्रसूश्चैव चागम्याष्टादश स्मृताः ॥ 54 ॥
4.78.m: maternal uncle's wife, a newly married woman, paternal uncle's wife, a menstruating woman, / and also the mother of one's father and mother: eighteen women are recorded as forbidden. // 54

4.78.s:
kīrtitāḥ sāmavede ca paripālyāḥ satāṃ vraja .
etā dṛṣṭvā ca spṛṣṭvā ca brahmahatyāṃ labhennaraḥ .. 55 ..
4.78.d:
कीर्तिताः सामवेदे च परिपाल्याः सतां व्रज ।
एता दृष्ट्वा च स्पृष्ट्वा च ब्रह्महत्यां लभेन्नरः ॥ 55 ॥
4.78.m: They are proclaimed in the Sāmaveda and must be guarded, O [lord of] Vraja, by the virtuous. / Having looked upon or touched these [forbidden women in lust], a man incurs the sin of Brahmin-murder. // 55

4.78.s:
tasmāddaivena tā dṛṣṭvā sūryaṃ dṛṣṭvā hariṃ smaret .
kāmato yadi paśyanti vinindyāste bhavanti vai .. 56 ..
4.78.d:
तस्माद्दैवेन ता दृष्ट्वा सूर्यं दृष्ट्वा हरिं स्मरेत् ।
कामतो यदि पश्यन्ति विनिन्द्यास्ते भवन्ति वै ॥ 56 ॥
4.78.m: Therefore, if one sees them by chance, one should look at the sun and remember Hari. / If they look upon them with desire, they indeed become utterly blameworthy. // 56

4.78.s:
tasmātsanto na paśyanti śāpabhītā vrajeśvara .
rāhugrastaṃ raviṃ sobhaṃ na paśyanti vipaścitaḥ .. 57 ..
4.78.d:
तस्मात्सन्तो न पश्यन्ति शापभीता व्रजेश्वर ।
राहुग्रस्तं रविं सोभं न पश्यन्ति विपश्चितः ॥ 57 ॥
4.78.m: Therefore, the virtuous do not look upon them, fearing a curse, O lord of Vraja. / Wise men do not gaze upon the sun or the moon eclipsed by Rāhu; // 57

4.78.s:
janmāṣṭasaptariḥ phāṅkadaśamasthe divākare .
janmarkṣe nidhane cāpi caturthe'pi kalānidhau .. 58 ..
4.78.d:
जन्माष्टसप्तरिः फाङ्कदशमस्थे दिवाकरे ।
जन्मर्क्षे निधने चापि चतुर्थेऽपि कलानिधौ ॥ 58 ॥
4.78.m: nor when the sun stands in the birth-sign, the eighth, the seventh, the twelfth, or the tenth, / nor when the moon is in the birth-asterism, in the eighth house, or also in the fourth. // 58

4.78.s:
sarvairaṃśairna paśyanti kampitaṃ candrabhāskaram .
neṣṭacandro na dṛśyaśya bhādre māsi sitāsite .. 59 ..
4.78.d:
सर्वैरंशैर्न पश्यन्ति कम्पितं चन्द्रभास्करम् ।
नेष्टचन्द्रो न दृश्यश्य भाद्रे मासि सितासिते ॥ 59 ॥
4.78.m: They do not view the eclipsed moon or sun in any of their parts. / The moon in the month of Bhādra, in both bright and dark [fortnights], is not to be looked upon. // 59

4.78.s:
caturthyāmuditaścandraḥ parityakto manīṣimiḥ .
candrastārāpaharaṇaṃ kalaṅgamatiduṣkaram .. 60 ..
4.78.d:
चतुर्थ्यामुदितश्चन्द्रः परित्यक्तो मनीषिमिः ।
चन्द्रस्तारापहरणं कलङ्गमतिदुष्करम् ॥ 60 ॥
4.78.m: The moon risen on the fourth day is shunned by the wise. / The moon gives the terrible stain of stealing Tārā // 60

4.78.s:
tasmai dadāti he nanda kāmato di paśyati .
